data.progTitle: MSc Physiotherapy (pre-registration) Full-time
data.shortTitle: MSc Physio (pre-reg) (SF) FT
aims: The programme offers a challenging and stimulating learning experience for graduates wishing to contribute to evolving healthcare needs through the practice of physiotherapy.  The key aim of the programme will be to facilitate the development of autonomous, competent and capable graduate physiotherapists exercising their own professional judgement with the potential to make a significant contribution to future healthcare services. This will centre on providing opportunities for students to develop and critically evaluate integrated knowledge and skills underpinning effective and safe physiotherapy practice that meets the legal and ethical boundaries of their profession. The course will be based on a philosophy of patient-centred care and respond appropriately to the needs of all different groups and individuals in a non-discriminatory and inclusive manner.

The expectations of the registered healthcare practitioner will be emphasised in terms of professional values, attitudes and behaviour commensurate with a registerable qualification. Approaches to practice will be grounded in evidence drawn from literature, policy and practice. Students will be provided with opportunities throughout this course to develop an in-depth understanding of evidence-based practice and research.  Acknowledgement of Birmingham as a research-led university will be evident with opportunities provided for students to participate in research activities in the school including the ability to conduct their own projects.

In addition, students will develop their clinical reasoning and decision-making skills informed by evidence-based practice and critical evaluation of these sources. Students will understand the value of a reflective practice which will enable them to develop greater self-awareness and independence in learning. The programme will continue to be responsive to changes in the socio-political environment and promote communication, teamwork, innovation and flexibility as key skills underpinning effective personal and professional development. Students will also have opportunities to engage with and contribute to the local community in promoting and preventing ill health during both university and practice-based learning activities.

On completion of the programme, graduates are in a position to apply for registration as a physiotherapist with the Health and Care Professions Council (HCPC) and as full members of the Chartered Society of Physiotherapy (CSP).
data.benchmark: Relevant Professional, statutory and regulatory bodies (PSRBs) used

outcome: 1. Key concepts of the biological, physical, social, psychological and clinical sciences underpinning the safe and effective practice of physiotherapy
2. The role of physiotherapy in the promotion, prevention and management of ill health and injury and the maintenance of health and well-being
3. Processes underpinning team working and communication as they affect inter-and intra-professional working and working with other professionals, clients/patients, carers and other service users.
4. Ethical, legal, moral and professional responsibilities of a physiotherapist as well as the skills and behaviours that reflect the HCPC and CSP attributes for a physiotherapist.
5. Performance framework and quality assurance mechanisms and standards  within physiotherapy practice
6. Clinical reasoning and decision making processes in physiotherapy providing a service which places the patient/client central to the therapeutic process.
7. Delivery and evaluation processes to provide effective person-centred care in a variety of contexts for people across the lifespan.
learning: All learning and teaching methods used in the programme contribute to students gaining one or more of the above

learning outcomes. Examples of those methods include lectures, evidence-based learning, problem-based learning, group work activities, e-learning using flipped classroom approach and creative activities, seminars, action learning sets, laboratory practicals, simulation events, guided independent study, field trips  and work-based placements, leadership and research-based practice activities and interdisciplinary learning activities.
assessment: Each assessment method aims to examine the level to which students have achieved one or more of the programme

learning outcomes.These include practical assessments including OSCE, essays, case study analyses, seminar presentations, poster presentations, critical and reflective portfolios and practice placement assessment forms.

outcome: 1. Independent and critical thinking skills to identify patient/client need and deliver safe and effective physiotherapy care in response to a contemporary patient-centred model of care
2. Ability to promote autonomy and enable patients/clients and groups to optimise health and social well-being through prevention, support, education and self-management
3. Create a resilient workforce with problem-solving skills, adaptability, flexibility and resourcefulness to meet the changing needs of future health care in a variety of settings.
4. Act consistently with their personal and professional values to support the well-being of themselves and others.
5. Work collegiately with a multi-disciplinary team of healthcare professionals and patients/clients in a manner consistent with the principles of anti-discriminatory and anti-oppressive practice.
6. Optimise healthcare using research skills and evidence-based healthcare to integrate results into clinical reasoning and decision-making enhancing the quality-of-service provision.
7. Become future-minded graduates and lifelong learners who can adapt to changing demands and promote continuous professional development.
learning: Lectures, evidence-based learning, problem-based learning, group work activities, e-learning using flipped classroom approach and creative activities, seminars, action learning sets, laboratory practicals, simulation events, guided independent study, work-based placements, leadership and research-based practice activities and interdisciplinary learning activities.

aims: The Anaesthesia Associate programme aims to develop a new practitioner who is able to safely fulfil a proportion of those roles currently only undertaken by anaesthetists. This new role is seen to be important in pioneering the shift of work, traditionally done only by doctors, to new, non-medically trained grades of staff. It also addresses the current workforce planning problems in anaesthesia.
In detail the aims of the programme are to develop:
? a `practitioner? role that enables the anaesthesia team to have more staff working in different ways under the supervision of the medically qualified anaesthetist.
? a cadre of non-medical practitioners who are motivated and competent to maintain patient safety, quality of care and outcomes.

? practitioners who are clear about the limits of their role, can present it transparently to  and can gain and maintain the confidence of, the public and those who manage, fund and work in the health service.
? professionals who have the motivation and intellectual capacity to make effective use of continuing education throughout their careers.
This programme allows students to extend their studies beyond the qualification required for registration (Diploma: Anaesthesia Associate to an MSc, by satisfactorily completing a dissertation).

aims: The programme aims to provide students with an understanding and appreciation of central areas of Philosophy, its methods and history.  It aims to engage their interest in and enthusiasm for issues of Philosophy and to foster within them the skills distinctive of good philosophy: in particular, the abilities to
analyse abstract claims and arguments accurately
present their own views verbally and in writing, clearly and with supporting argument
collaborate with others in the course of such analyses and presentations

The programme aims to provide students with the opportunity to engage with the range of expertise and internationally recognized research undertaken in the Dept. of Philosophy. Through these various aims and provisions, the programme will enrich the lives of students who take it, and will provide society with the resource of graduates who can think and express their thoughts in a clear and logical manner. Graduates equipped with these transferable skills as well as with the knowledge of the subject's contents will be employed in a wide range of occupations.
For Year Abroad programme only:
In addition to the aims of the 3-year philosophy BA programme, the 4-year programme has aims to:
To give students the opportunity to live in the society and culture of a foreign country
To provide the opportunity to learn a foreign language/improve existing proficiency (where applicable)
To acquire the ability to study authors of interest in their original language (where applicable)
To provide the opportunity to experience academic life in general, and philosophy in particular, as it is practised in another country
To enhance students' organisation and communication skills
To enhance students' employability through proven ability to succeed in a foreign setting
To provide an extra opportunity for students to study in more depth topics of particular interest to them.
For Year in Computer Science programme only:

Computer Science is both an academic discipline in its own right and an enabling technology for other disciplines: Arts, Humanities and Social Sciences as well as Science and Engineering. The focus here is firmly on Computer Science as an enabling technology. The programme aims to provide a solid, self-contained and coherent core of computer science suitable for combination with a variety of other academic disciplines. It aims to provide:
A grounding in the theory underpinning modern developments in computer science.
An introduction to practical software design and implementation.
A range of options in computer science to cater for a variety of interests and backgrounds.

outcome: The texts, theories and arguments of some of the major analytical philosophers, both past and present.
Some central theories and arguments in most of the core areas of analytical philosophy (metaphysics, epistemology, philosophy of mind, and moral and political philosophy).
Some theories and arguments that are the subject of current research in contemporary analytical philosophy.
A range of techniques of philosophical reasoning, and how those techniques are brought to bear on philosophical theories and problems.
Basic logical notation and proof procedures, and of the most important ways in which those techniques inform analytic philosophy in general.
learning: lectures; seminar discussions; close, crucial reading and discussion of texts; the design and construction of essays and other assessments
assessment: Exams, essays, coursework exercises and project work

The ability to present cogent arguments in defence of their philosophical views, verbally and in writing.

The ability to work independently, including devising and researching  pieces of philosophical writing of various lengths - and in groups.
The capacity to be competent and effective users of IT resources for research purposes, word processing. Students will also be able to use IT communication tools effectively.

To develop a range of marketable skills including problem solving, communication, patience and perseverance, determination, self-motivation, analytical and study skills through direct interactions with society and institutions in another country.

aims: The programme aims to develop students? enthusiasm for Earth studies in the broadest sense, to produce graduates with professional skills of observation, critical evaluation, deduction and reporting, and to encourage a habit of maintaining personal competence through study.  Geology and geography have a continuously evolving knowledge base of history and process, rooted in observation of inevitably incomplete and diverse data sets, and given theoretical coherence by an interdisciplinary scientific framework.  In this programme, whose geological content is combined equally with modules provided in Geography & Environmental Sciences, there is a particular focus on Earth's surface processes and environments and the ways these interact with human activities.  The integrated knowledge, understanding and skills acquired fit graduates for careers and/or further study in both geology and geography, particularly in environmental areas, and are appropriate also to a wider field of graduate employment.  The School of Geography, Earth & Environmental Sciences at the University of Birmingham undertakes a wide range of research in the component disciplines, and offers a variety of taught programmes.  The Lapworth Museum, with around half a million geological specimens, is an integral part of the School, and provides a valuable resource for learning and teaching as well as for research.  The Geology & Geography programme provides a broad-based scientific education, integrating material from other major scientific subjects with specifically geological and geographical concepts and skills.  No previous knowledge of geology is assumed.  Fieldwork forms a significant and integral part of the programme, occupying some 30 days.  The structure of the programme ensures that all students are able to develop core knowledge, understanding and skills, but its modular nature allows individuals to develop an academic profile most suited to their particular interests and aptitudes.  Independent project work comprises a major part of the programme, and forms the basis for more than a third of the final BSc classification.

aims: The programme provides students the opportunity to explore the diversity of Greek and Roman culture, drawing together literature, drama, myth, religion, history, philosophy, and art. Students will analyse a wide range of evidence (material, written, digital) in a critical manner. The programme allows students to explore the interconnected nature of Greek and Roman societies with each other and other cultures of the Mediterranean and beyond. The Classical Studies programme contributes to students? understanding of the origins of modern culture, enabling students to engage critically with the Classical world and its impact on the modern world.
The programme aims to::
facilitate intellectual development by encouraging independence and critical thinking.
provide a foundation for research into and further study of the Classical world.

To develop an innovative range of subject specific and transferable skills in research, analysis and presentation through the study and understanding of Classical Studies in the context of cognate disciplines.

develop an innovative range of subject specific and transferable skills in research, analysis and presentation through the study and understanding of Classical studies in the context of cognate disciplines.
instil sensitivity to the range of cultural similarities and differences that is of particular importance and value in modern multicultural societies.
provide the opportunity to study relevant ancient languages.
provide the broadest possible platform of transferable skills for both further study and intellectual training outside the Academy

Graduates of the Classical Studies programme have wide career prospects, including academic research, teaching (from primary to higher education), the creative economy, and government work. Some of these career paths may require further studies.
For Year/ Semester Abroad programmes only:

The year/ semester abroad will provide students with the opportunity to immerse themselves in the society and culture of a foreign country while gaining experience of a different academic environment and way of teaching. The year abroad also provides an opportunity for students to improve their existing language proficiency (where applicable) as well as enhancing their organisation and communication skills and their employability through a proven ability to succeed in a foreign setting. It also provides students with the opportunity to understand the approaches to the past and methodologies for its study employed in other countries or cultures.

outcome: A core sample of Classical literature within its cultural and intellectual context
Critical and hermeneutic issues specific to the discipline of Classics
Classical civilisation in its original context through study and personal experience
In addition, students have the opportunity to have knowledge and understanding of an ancient classical language and some ancient texts
Year/ Semester Abroad only  Demonstrate the ability to study relevant topics at an international institution and appreciate the difference between study in the UK and overseas.
learning: 1-4. Lectures, seminars, workshops, group project work, oral presentations, language classes, (for BA only) independent research (dissertation)
5. Year abroad/ Semester Abroad
assessment: 1 - 4. Examinations, extended essays, dissertation, seminar presentation, group work, commentaries, reviews and other appropriate assessments
5. Year Abroad/ Semester Abroad Module (assessment as required by host institution).

outcome: Ability to summarise, synthesise, analyse and evaluate others? arguments, and to formulate their own logical and structured arguments, normally both orally and in writing, with appropriate supporting evidence.
Research, describe and analyse primary evidence and construct an informed synthesis from it in relation to current knowledge

Independent study skills (self-organisation, initiative and self-direction; time management; autonomous research skills; the ability to collect, organise, synthesise and evaluate information; planning, drafting and editing)
The ability to produce an extended piece of academic writing, drawing on independent study skills acquired on the programme.

Ability to work as a member of a team in a range of contexts, including the capacity to listen, to respond flexibly to feedback, to understand diverse perspectives, and to negotiate solutions collectively
Identify problems and questions and critically evaluate solutions and answers in theoretical and practical aspects of research into the ancient world

Transferable skills relevant to employment, including problem-solving, self-reliance, initiative, adaptability, flexibility, resilience, self-motivation, and competences such as note-taking, the ability to work under pressure and meet deadlines, ability to use and manipulate digital resources and to present information and ideas effectively using ICT.

aims: This programme provides students with a diversity of skills with hands-on expertise in utilising healthcare data suited to the needs of future health data scientists, enabling them to perform analyses and develop novel tools and methods for this rapidly growing field. It is aimed at students with diverse backgrounds from biomedical/medical domains, including clinical trainees, as well as Computer Sciences, Mathematics and Statistics to conduct their own analyses, and also to create the next generation of cutting-edge health data scientists who will be able to develop new tools and methods matching the latest technological advancements

Students will learn about the breadth of the fields of health data science, from medicine and biology, over ethics and health care systems, to mathematical modelling and computer sciences. They will be able to design, perform and enhance analyses with the appropriate methods and technologies to address practical medical and clinical questions.

This program fits well within the University and College strategies to increase postgraduate programmes that enhance education and research capabilities in the health data and biosciences. Further, playing a role in the creation of the next generation of bioinformaticians will improve the University's standings as a global leader in biomedical research.

data.progTitle: MEng Mechanical Engineering with a Year Abroad Full-time
data.shortTitle: MEng Mech Eng Year Abr FT
data.longTitle: Mechanical Engineering with a Year Abroad
aims: The Educational Aims of the Programme are to:

a) Provide a professionally accredited course of study that is of comparable standard to those offered by other leading European universities, that will attract high quality students, irrespective of race, background, gender or physical disability both from within the UK and from overseas

b) Educate students to MEng (Hons) level, accredited as meeting in full the educational/knowledge and understanding requirement for CEng registration as detailed in the Accreditation of Higher Education Programmes (Fourth Edition) (AHEP4)

c) Provide students with a thorough knowledge of engineering principles, concepts and mathematics and with practice at using their understanding to formulate and solve complex problems in mechanical engineering
d) Provide students with a depth of specialised knowledge within a research environment and develop their critical analysis and thinking skills
e) Provide students with international experience through spending a year abroad

f) Enable students to develop the skills necessary to engage in, plan and successfully complete individual and team design projects, and appreciate the economic, social, environmental, ethical and commercial context of their decisions

g) Produce engineering graduates equipped to play leading roles in industry, the professions and public service, and with the intellectual abilities and transferable skills necessary to further their professional development by personal research or study in preparation for a career as a registered professional engineer.

outcome: By the end of the programme students will have knowledge and understanding in the specific areas of learning of - Science and Mathematics, Engineering Analysis, Design and Innovation, The Engineer and Society, and Engineering Practice as required by AHEP 4th Edition (Learning outcomes M1-M18). They will specifically have knowledge and understanding of;

1. Mathematics, statistics, natural science and engineering principles for the solution of complex problems in the field of Mechanical Engineering. Much of the knowledge will be at the forefront of the particular subject of study and informed by a critical awareness of new developments and the wider context of engineering. [related to M1]
2. How to formulate and analyse complex problems in Mechanical Engineering to reach substantiated conclusions, and understanding of the limitations of the techniques employed. [related to M2]
3. Computational and analytical techniques relevant to modelling complex Mechanical Engineering problems, and an understanding of their limitations. [related to M3]
4. Sources of technical literature and other sources of information to solve complex problems in Mechanical Engineering. [related to M4]
5. How a combination of societal, user, business and customer needs are used to design solutions for complex problems in Mechanical Engineering. [related to M5]
6. Integrated or systems approaches to the solution of complex problems in Mechanical Engineering. [related to M6]
7. The environmental and societal impact of Mechanical Engineering solutions to complex problems and how to minimise adverse impact. [related to M7]
8. Ethics in Mechanical Engineering practice and professional codes of conduct. [related to M8]
9. Risk management and mitigations processes for Mechanical Engineering projects. [related to M9]
10. Holistic approaches to the mitigation of security risks. [related to M10]
11. Inclusive approaches to engineering practice and the benefits and importance of supporting equality, diversity and inclusion. [related to M11]
12. A range of practical laboratory and workshop suitable for investigating complex mechanical engineering problems. [related to M12]
13. Materials, equipment, engineering technologies and processes, that are appropriate for use in solutions of mechanical engineering problems. [related to M13]
14. Quality management systems and continuous improvement processes that can be applied to the management of complex problems in mechanical engineering. [related to M14]

15. Engineering management principles, commercial context, project and change management, and relevant legal matters including intellectual property rights that would be relevant to mechanical engineering. [related to M15]
16. The principles of effective team working including team leadership, and tools/processes for monitoring effectiveness of a team. [relates to M16]
17. Effective communication techniques for different audiences and understanding of methods for evaluating effectiveness of the communication. [relates to M17]
18. Methods for planning and recording self-learning and development, and the importance of CPD. [relates to M18]
learning: Lectures, Tutorials, Problem Solving Classes, Exercise classes, Seminars, Computer Laboratories, Laboratory Experiments, Design Projects, Group Projects, Team working, Individual Projects, Practical work and Workshop training, and Independent study
assessment: Exams, Coursework, Reports, Essays, Online Assessments/Quizzes, Class Tests, Individual and Group based Design Projects, Computer Modelling Assignments, Work Sheets, Presentations/Posters/Video Presentations, and Prototype Manufacture.

outcome: By the end of the programme they will have the skills and other attributes to be able to;

1. Apply a comprehensive knowledge of mathematics, statistics, natural science and engineering principles to the solution of complex problems. Much of the knowledge will be at the forefront of the particular subject of study and informed by a critical awareness of new developments and the wider context of engineering. [M1]

2. Formulate and analyse complex problems to reach substantiated conclusions. This will involve evaluating available data using first principles of mathematics, statistics, natural science and engineering principles, and using engineering judgment to work with information that may be uncertain or incomplete, discussing the limitations of the techniques employed. [M2]
3. Select and apply appropriate computational and analytical techniques to model complex problems, discussing the limitations of the techniques employed. [M3]
4. Select and critically evaluate technical literature and other sources of information to solve complex problems. [M4]

5. Design solutions for complex problems that evidence some originality and meet a combination of societal, user, business and customer needs as appropriate. This will involve consideration of applicable health and safety, diversity, inclusion, cultural, societal, environmental and commercial matters, codes of practice and industry standards. [M5]
6. Apply an integrated or systems approach to the solution of complex problems. [M6]
7. Evaluate the environmental and societal impact of solutions to complex problems (to include the entire lifecycle of a product or process) and minimise adverse impacts. [M7]
8. Identify and analyse ethical concerns and make reasoned ethical choices informed by professional codes of conduct. [M8]
9. Use a risk management process to identify, evaluate and mitigate risks (the effects of uncertainty) associated with a particular project or activity. [M9]
10. Adopt a holistic and proportionate approach to the mitigation of security risks. [M10]
11. Adopt an inclusive approach to engineering practice and recognise the responsibilities, benefits and importance of supporting equality, diversity and inclusion. [M11]
12. Use practical laboratory and workshop skills to investigate complex problems. [M12]
13. Select and apply appropriate materials, equipment, engineering technologies and processes, recognising their limitations. [M13]
14. Discuss the role of quality management systems and continuous improvement in the context of complex problems. [M14]
15. Apply knowledge of engineering management principles, commercial context, project and change management, and relevant legal matters including intellectual property rights. [M15]
16. Function effectively as an individual, and as a member or leader of a team. Evaluate effectiveness of own and team performance. [M16]
17. Communicate effectively on complex engineering matters with technical and non-technical audiences, evaluating the effectiveness of the methods used. [M17]
18. Plan and record self-learning and development as the foundation for lifelong learning/CPD. [M18]
learning: Team Working, Individual and Team Projects, Coursework Assignments, Lectures, Tutorials, Seminars, Computer Laboratory, Practical work and Workshop training, and Independent study.
assessment: Coursework, Reports, Essays, Individual and Team Presentations, Design & Build, Computer Tests, Computer Modelling Assignment, Presentations, and Exams

Additionally, to progress to Stage III of MEng Mechanical Engineering with a Year Abroad, a student is required to have passed all credits and to have a Stage II average mark of at least 59.5%. aims: The psychology component of the programme aims to provide a broad, fundamental and practical education in the discipline of psychology which is informed by staff research interests.  This is achieved by i) covering approaches to the study of psychology which range from the observations of basic neural mechanisms to the analysis of complex human relationships including those in an applied setting, and ii) interpreting contemporary empirical findings from a series of different theoretically grounded perspectives.The programme involves:i)  coverage of the core areas of psychology, that is biological, cognitive, developmental, personality and individual differences, and social psychology.Ii) training in research methods leading to competence in research design, data collection, analysis, statistics, interpretation and report writing,iii) in depth study of optional specialised topics which are at the cutting edge of research.  Students are thus equipped with discipline-specific knowledge to appreciate and critically evaluate theory, research findings and their applications; to undertake independent, supervised research and to acquire transferable, employment related skills.On completion of the programme students have the skills and necessary preparation for both professional training, the degree being recognised by the British Psychological Society as conferring the Graduate Basis for Registration, and further academic study.

aims: The programme is managed by the EPSRC funded Centre for Doctoral Training in Formulation Engineering.  The Centre integrates the interdisciplinary expertise of the component schools (Engineering (Chemical Engineering and Materials Science), Physics and Chemistry) aimed at formulation of multiphase structured products in a wide variety of forms.

The programme focuses on research into the physical, chemical and biological processes that create product structure, and the maintenance or breakdown of that structure in use. An important feature of the approach is that it is focused on achieving the desired performance of the product and the means to achieve this, rather than on characterisation of existing processes. This is a different approach from the traditional one in chemical engineering, and places new demands on interdisciplinarity and innovation.

Students will take an inherently multidisciplinary approach, involving the component disciplines of Chemical Engineering, Materials Science, Chemistry, Physics and Biosciences, to a largely undeveloped area. The intention is to develop a framework of understanding for the design, manufacture and performance assessment of formulated products.

Students will develop personal, scientific and business skills to enable them to carry out the joint industry-academia research programme. The programme aims to produce graduates able to take charge of development teams in the most competitive markets.
Previous graduates have progressed to work within the formulation engineering sector, with many continuing employment at their sponsor companies.

aims: "This programme provides students with an understanding of economic concepts, principles and tools, and their application. The programme aims to stimulate students intellectually through the study of economics and to lead them to appreciate its application to a range of problems and its relevance in a variety of contexts. Students should receive a firm foundation of knowledge about the workings of economic systems and develop the relevant skills for the constructive use of that knowledge in a range of settings.

The first year of the programme provides a foundation in economics and develops the main quantitative tools required through the programme. The second year develops a core of Microeconomics, Macroeconomics and Econometrics, alongside more specialised policy-based and theoretical modules. In the final year of the programme, there is increased flexibility to specialise in a number of theoretical and policy-oriented fields.

aims: This programme aims to develop the intellectual, analytical and communication skills of students by providing them with a breadth of knowledge of Psychology with Business Management, together with the transferable skills (for example in group and team working) that are necessary to apply this knowledge in new and challenging contexts. The underlying philosophy of the programme is that students study many aspects of Psychology and develop a speciality in Business Management.
The proposed Business Management pathway aims to equip students with specialized skills while still allowing them to gain broad-based knowledge from other themes offered within the Psychology degree.

Consultations with employers revealed that while they value graduates with the broad based knowledge that our graduates bring to their graduate trainee schemes, they also place great emphasis on graduates with specialties in Psychology, having an in depth knowledge of relevant  skills, being conversant with digital platforms and research competencies (both qualitative and quantitative). The Business Management pathway is designed to give such competences and skills to the students so that they are better prepared for the job market. Furthermore, given the fact that psychology and business is conducted today in a global environment and that it is necessary to be able to interact with other markets and cultures, an international underpinning is to be found in this programme.

The programme aims to provide a broad, fundamental and practical education in the discipline of psychology which is informed by staff research interests and requirements for careers in psychological research.  This is achieved by (i) covering approaches to the study of psychology which range from the observations of basic neural mechanisms to the analysis of complex human relationships including those in an applied setting, and (ii) interpreting contemporary empirical findings from a series of different theoretically grounded perspectives.  The programme involves: (i) coverage of the core areas of psychology, that is biological, cognitive, developmental, personality and individual differences, and social psychology, (ii) training in research methods leading to competence in research design, data collection, analysis, statistics, interpretation and report writing, (iii) in depth study of optional specialised topics which are at the cutting edge of research.

Students are thus equipped with discipline-specific knowledge to appreciate and critically evaluate theory, research findings and their applications; to undertake independent, supervised research and to acquire transferable, employment related skills.  On completion of the programme students have the skills and necessary preparation for both professional training and further academic study being aligned to the British Psychological Society, allowing graduates to seek Graduate Basis for Registration.

The programme also progresses an understanding of the role of individuals and business in society. It develops effective problem-solving skills and an ability to communicate well using a range of media. The programme recognises the increasing role of business in society and so develops knowledge of ethical issues and practices across the discipline whilst evolving awareness of individual and collective citizenship as a part of responsible business.
Each year of the programme has 80 credits of Psychology modules and 40 credits of Business Management modules.

aims: This postgraduate programme enables you to develop your knowledge of the inter-related fields of art history and curating. The programme is delivered through a combination of theoretical and practical approaches to understanding and curating historic and contemporary art in a variety of global contexts.

As part of the core curating modules, you will be introduced to critical approaches in curating and develop your understanding of curatorial concepts and methods, such as the role of the curator, institutional contexts, and text and interpretation. You will then work in collaboration with one of the programme's partner institutions, and in student groups, to develop and deliver a real-world curatorial project in a professional context. You will gain a range of skills relevant to each project and to the wider sector, such as collaborative practice, display, public programming and marketing.

The core module on the history of art and visual culture equips you with methods for understanding and analysing artworks, drawing on historical and contemporary approaches.  The core research training module provides a theoretical and practical foundation for your studies, from researching sources to developing a dissertation proposal. aims: BA Drama and Film is characterised by a wide study, which is methodologically- and theoretically- informed, of Film, ranging across genres, modes and media, combined with the theoretical and practical exploration of a wide range of theatrical and performance styles, from British playwrights and actor training to immersive practices and directing.

Students will develop a deep and rich understanding of the generative, compositional and self-reflective processes involved in creative work in both disciplines, learning practical, technical and industry-specific skills en route. Students will also engage critically with the history and thematic dimensions of both disciplines, encountering a wide range of approaches to Drama and Film in different historical periods. In the third year, students will have the opportunity to take the Professional Skills Module, to undertake a placement or progress their own entrepreneurial project.
The programme aims to produce individuals who possess a broad range of knowledge and understanding of Drama and Film. It will give students the opportunity to:
Develop analytical and practical skills derived from close reading of a wide range of film and performance texts and informed by critical studies
Understand different modes of representation on stage and on film, and how they are socially and politically informed
Gain skills in writing, reasoning, presentation, performance and independent research
Work creatively through film and performance practices to explore a diversity of ways of engaging different audiences
Understand the histories and practices of film-making and performance, underpinned by key theoretical approaches
Develop interpersonal and communication skills, with particular strengths in collaboration and teamwork
Gain an understanding of how to narrate these skills to future employers.

The wide range of reasoning, research, independent learning, communication and creative skills acquired from this programme equips graduates to pursue further study or employment in Drama and Film related disciplines, and is readily transferable to a variety of commercial, cultural and professional careers, including the creative arts, film or media sectors.

aims: The MA Educational Leadership & Management is designed to develop specialised knowledge and skills in educational theories, policies and practices. A series of core modules equip you with an economic, historical, philosophical and sociological framework for understanding the field of education and with the skills required for conducting critical research. Evidence for the effects of teaching and school organisation on student's learning will be reviewed, and you will be equipped to use this evidence base for developing both your own practice, and that of others, in the institution in which you work. You will also develop reflective and critical judgement of educational professionals and learn how to deploy these skills in the interests of improving teacher effectiveness and leading institutional change.

The programme will be of particular interest to education practitioners, and policymakers, researchers and administrators who are seeking to promote school effectiveness and to lead change in a manner consistent with educational inclusion and equity. The focus on critical analysis and evidence-based outcomes will be especially attractive to those who are, or who anticipate being, in positions to lead change. Specifically, the programme will enable students to:
Explain key concepts and themes in the field of education and apply them to practice in a range of contexts;
Explain and critique current debates in the field of educational leadership using concepts from the disciplines of economics, history, philosophy and sociology;
Identify and appraise educational practices that promote inclusion and equity;
Critically analyse and evaluate research evidence for school improvement;
Develop reflective and critical judgement of educational professionals and other stakeholders committed to the interests of all children;
Develop capacity for rigorous and critical analysis of evidence in improving schools;
Promote critical engagement and fulfilling learning environments by developing teacher effectiveness and professional identity;
Develop communities of scholarship through which educational partnerships work to improve schooling and schooling policy;
Identify and explain the characteristics of critical and ethical research;
Interpret, assess and deploy research methodologies;
Translate knowledge gained from reading, discussion and writing into the analysis of educational policy and practice;
Contribute to the informed construction of educational policy which underpin educational practices;
Gain a critical understanding of approaches to research.

aims: Biotechnology is an interdisciplinary field spanning the biosciences and is going to play a key role in responding to many global issues. It has been at the forefront of some of the most ground-breaking discoveries and innovations in recent years. From developing novel therapies for diseases to designing genetically modified organisms with enhanced traits; and continues to push the boundaries of what is possible in science and medicine. Key disciplines linked to biotechnology include genetics, cell biology, plants sciences, chemistry and chemical engineering. Advances in biotechnology play an important role in shaping various industries and improving the overall quality of life. Biotechnology graduates will benefit from a wide and diverse range of careers and opportunities.

With a growing global population, ensuring food security and sustainable agricultural practices is, and will continue to be, crucial. Although controversial, biotechnology is important for agricultural sustainability with a key role in developing genetically modified crops that are resistant to pests, droughts, and diseases, thereby increasing yield and reducing the environmental impact of farming.

Biotechnology contributes to environmental conservation by offering solutions to pollution, waste management, and the development of renewable energy sources. Biotechnology graduates will contribute to the creation of cleaner and more sustainable technologies.

Biotechnology has and will continue to be a key discipline in the healthcare revolution by enabling the development of precision medicine, gene therapies, and advanced diagnostic tools. Biotechnology undergraduates will develop the knowledge and skills to allow them to contribute to the development of new treatments and technologies within a healthcare setting.

Industries such as pharmaceuticals, biofuels, and bioplastics rely on biotechnological processes to manufacture products efficiently and sustainably. Graduates with a biotechnology degree can work in a variety of sectors and contribute to the development of greener and more efficient industrial processes.

The proposed biotechnology programme will provide students with a diverse skill set that includes biology, chemistry, genetics, microbiology, bioinformatics, and possible engineering. This interdisciplinary approach will develop and enhance problem-solving abilities of our students and prepare graduates to tackle complex challenges from multiple angles. In addition, biotechnology involves discussions about the ethical implications of certain technologies, such as gene editing and cloning and therefore students will be exposed to these ethical discussions, preparing them to navigate complex ethical dilemmas in their future career.

Both the BSc and MSci programme will provide the students with the opportunity to develop their research expertise during the research project and for professional placement students in an industrial setting.

Biotechnology has a global impact, addressing challenges that affect people's lives worldwide, such as disease outbreaks, environmental degradation, and food shortages. Biotechnology graduates will contribute to solving these global issues. Many breakthroughs in biotechnology have led to the creation of successful start-up companies. With the right knowledge and skills, graduates can become entrepreneurs and drive innovation in the biotech industry.

data.shortTitle: MSc Clinical Exercise Scien FT
aims: The MSc in Clinical Exercise Physiology is designed to provide a comprehensive and in-depth understanding of the role of exercise in the prevention, treatment, and management of chronic diseases and conditions. This programme integrates advanced theoretical knowledge with practical skills, preparing graduates to excel in a rapidly evolving healthcare environment.

Overview of the Programme and its Content: This innovative programme offers a blend of cutting-edge coursework, practical experiences, and research opportunities. Students will engage with modules covering a wide range of topics, including advanced exercise physiology, clinical assessment techniques, intervention design and delivery, and behaviour change. The curriculum is distinguished by its focus on evidence-based practice and its integration of interdisciplinary approaches, combining insights from physiology, psychology, and healthcare. Innovative elements of the programme include hands-on clinical placements, state-of-the-art laboratory sessions, and the use of simulation technology to enhance learning outcomes. The programme also emphasises the development of critical thinking and problem-solving skills through a comprehensive dissertation project and viva examination.
Skills and Experiences: Students enrolled in the MSc in Clinical Exercise Physiology will develop a broad spectrum of skills essential for clinical practice and research. These include:

Clinical Assessment Skills:Proficiency in conducting and interpreting a variety of clinical assessments, including cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET), electrocardiograms (ECG), and functional capacity evaluations.
Intervention Design and Implementation:Ability to design, implement, and evaluate personalised exercise programmes tailored to the needs of individuals with various health conditions.
Research and Analytical Skills: Competence in conducting rigorous scientific research, including data collection, analysis, and interpretation.

Professional Communication: Effective communication skills for interacting with patients, healthcare providers, and multidisciplinary teams, including the ability to convey complex information clearly and empathetically.
Critical Thinking and Problem-Solving: Advanced critical thinking and problem-solving abilities, enabling students to address complex clinical scenarios and make informed decisions.

Areas of Work or Further Study:Graduates of the MSc in Clinical Exercise Physiology will be well-prepared for a variety of career paths and further study opportunities. Potential areas of work include::
Clinical Exercise Physiologist: Working in NHS hospitals, rehabilitation centres, or private practice, designing and supervising exercise programmes for patients with chronic diseases.
Research Scientist: Conducting research in academic, clinical, or industry settings, contributing to the advancement of knowledge in exercise physiology and related fields.
Health Promotion Specialist: Developing and implementing community-based health and wellness programmes aimed at disease prevention and health improvement.
PhD Programmes: Pursuing further academic research and specialization through doctoral studies in exercise physiology, sport and exercise science, or related disciplines.
Healthcare Administration: Taking on roles in healthcare management and policy development, influencing the integration of exercise-based interventions into standard care practices.

Overall, this programme aims to equip students with the expertise and confidence to become leaders in the field of clinical exercise physiology, making significant contributions to patient care, research, and public health.

outcome: Demonstrate a deep understanding of the physiological, psychological, social, behavioural, and cultural factors that influence health status and the role of exercise and physical activity interventions in managing acute, sub-acute, chronic, and complex conditions.
Explain the impact of various diseases, disorders, and medications on acute exercise responses and chronic adaptations to exercise and physical activity interventions.
Interpret and apply evidence-based tools for assessing and monitoring clinical status and functional capacity in individuals with diverse health conditions.
Evaluate the effectiveness of exercise-based programs through evidence-based monitoring methods and adjust interventions as needed to optimise outcomes for individuals and groups.

Demonstrate a comprehensive understanding of the scope of practice for a Clinical Exercise Physiologist (CEP), including their role in prescribing and delivering evidence-based exercise interventions to optimise physical function and health across the care pathway from primary prevention to rehabilitation & maintenance.

Students are able to study linked perspectives that cross traditional disciplinary divides offering new analytical insight into 21st Century society.

A major strength of the programme is the opportunity for students to focus their studies on specific areas while at the same time gaining a solid understanding of associated processes. data.shortTitle: BA Relig w Psychol w Yr Abr FT
data.longTitle: Religion with Psychology with Year Abroad
aims: This is a unique interdisciplinary degree programme across the departments of Theology and Religion and Psychology.  Historically, there has been little cross-over between these two disciplines; however, the Psychology of Religion is a rapidly growing area of research, scholarship and public interest. The psychology of religion and belief is increasingly prominent in discussions of wellbeing and social change, and has an impact on several policy fields ranging from health service provision to security and counter-terrorism.

Despite this increase in research, scholarship and public interest, however, there are few opportunities for undergraduate students to directly engage with this area of study.  The programme fills this gap in the academic market, and appeal to students with varied interests, including:
Counselling/pastoral care/well-being interests
Psychology, religion and society
Psychology and Biblical studies
Psychology of religion research

This programme capitalizes on the range of expertise at the University of Birmingham, in theology and religion, psychology, and psychology of religion, as well as related areas such as the social scientific study of religion across several traditions (e.g., Islam, Sikhism, Christianity).  This programme is nationally and internationally unique at the undergraduate level, and will be of interest to students who are interested in interdisciplinary study which addresses many of the important issues at the heart of the human experience.
For Year Abroad programme only

This route offers students the additional educational benefit of a year of study in an approved overseas University. During the year abroad, students continue to develop and consolidate their knowledge and skills. In particular (and depending on where they go) this part of the programme is likely to expose them to different areas of expertise, contexts and approaches that will complement those they encounter in Birmingham, and this exposure should help them to develop a more balanced, multi-faceted appreciation of the subject.

aims: The programme aims to develop the intellectual, analytical and communication skills of students by providing them with a breadth of knowledge of business management, together with the transferable skills (for example in group and team working) that are necessary to apply this knowledge in new and challenging contexts.
The underlying philosophy of the programme is that students study all aspects of business management throughout the course and do not become overly specialised.

This generalist approach follows the approach that has always underpinned the UK Business suite of programmes, and has been used successfully in marketing these programmes in the past. In consultations with employers we are told that they value the broad-based knowledge that our graduates bring to their graduate trainee schemes.

Given the fact that business is conducted today in a global environment and that it is necessary to be able to interact with other markets and cultures, an international underpinning is to be found in most modules. In addition, an appreciation of other contemporary issues such as digital marketing, international entrepreneurship and management strategy is provided throughout the programme, which will also endeavor to impart a sense of corporate social responsibility.

Entry to the suite of BSc programmes in Dubai is into year one (stage 1). Year one provides a foundation in the core disciplines of business  and introduces the key themes of the programme. E.g. marketing, organisational behaviour, accounting and finance, economics and entrepreneurship. Year 1 also contains a key skills module for personal and academic development. Students are given a thorough grounding in the subject areas that they continue in later years. The modules studied will mirror the UK programme.

In Stage Two we adopt a generalist approach although modules begin to become more focused and specialized. The modules on the programme mirror those modules already offered in the UK based programme. The modules have been chosen as the most appropriate modules for the coherence of the programme, and the most suitable for the Dubai market for e.g. Services and Retail Strategy, that sits well with the nature of retail markets in Dubai, Intermediate Business Economics and Macro Economy, that allows room to contextualise the UAE economy in general and Dubai's macro economy in particular. Further modules such as Accounting, Management and Accountability that is suitable to offer discussions related to local context of accounting.

aims: This programme is a STEM-based MSc in sustainable energy engineering. Students will study a wide range of modules, starting with an introduction to the basic scientific and engineering principles underpinning the subject, and then building knowledge and application through technical (science/engineering) skills, data and digitisation, industrial applications, energy systems, and law/policy frameworks. The modules will reflect and focus on the energy research expertise of the Birmingham Energy Institute (BEI) and School of Chemical Engineering - for example, cooling, fuel cells, energy storage, and whole energy systems.

A key skillset developed in this programme is making decisions about complex data to drive forward innovations in energy. This could be implementing novel energy generation processes, choosing the best way to transmit or store energy, or developing ways to integrate energy generation, storage, and use.

Students will take 2 compulsory modules and then select a further 4 optional modules from a wide range of modules that reflect the research interests of School / BEI staff, thus enabling students to select a combination that reflect their specific interests.
Finally, students will undertake an independent original research project supervised by a member of BEI.

outcome: Demonstrate a comprehensive understanding of the core scientific principles underpinning sustainable energy engineering, including thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, heat transfer, and material science, in the context of renewable energy technologies.

Critically analyse the characteristics and interdependencies within energy systems, demonstrating an advanced understanding of systems engineering principles and their application to sustainable energy solutions.

Evaluate the policy and regulatory frameworks governing sustainable energy development and implementation at national and international levels, including their impact on technological innovation and market adoption.

Apply advanced research methodologies to locate, critically evaluate, and synthesise information from diverse sources, including academic literature, industry reports, and policy documents, to address complex challenges in sustainable energy engineering.

Apply appropriate modelling and simulation techniques to analyse and predict the performance of various energy systems components, including renewable energy sources, storage technologies, and energy conversion processes.
learning: Lectures, tutorials, seminars, problem classes, projects.
assessment: Written unseen examinations, open book examinations, computer-based examinations written reports, oral presentations, group design reports, individual design reports.

outcome: Critically evaluate the performance of diverse energy systems using appropriate analytical and modelling techniques, interpreting results to identify opportunities for optimisation and innovation.

Apply sustainability principles to assess the environmental and socio-economic impacts of energy systems, utilising appropriate metrics and life cycle analysis to evaluate and compare different technologies and strategies.

Utilise advanced computer-aided engineering tools and software to design, simulate, and optimise sustainable energy systems, effectively processing and visualising data to communicate findings to diverse audiences.

Effectively plan and manage independent research projects, demonstrating initiative, time management skills, and adaptability to overcome challenges and meet deadlines within the context of sustainable energy engineering.

Demonstrate a commitment to ethical conduct and professional responsibility in sustainable energy engineering, adhering to safety regulations and promoting sustainable practices in all aspects of their work.

Communicate complex technical and commercial information effectively through written reports, oral presentations, and visual media, tailoring communication style and content to diverse audiences in the field of sustainable energy.

Critically evaluate current research and advanced scholarship in sustainable energy engineering, demonstrating an ability to synthesise information and contribute to the advancement of knowledge in the field.
learning: Lectures, tutorials, seminars, problem classes, projects, computer-based workshops.
assessment: Effectively plan and manage independent research projects, demonstrating initiative, time management skills, and adaptability to overcome challenges and meet deadlines within the context of sustainable energy engineering. aims: "The LLB Law programme provides a broad education about law and legal processes in England and Wales and the European Union and the constitution of the United Kingdom. The study of law equips students with knowledge and skills for a variety of careers - including in the legal professions, public sector and commercial organisations. For students seeking to become practising lawyers in England and Wales or Northern Ireland, the LLB Law degree currently gives exemption from the first stage of professional examinations.

Students are exposed to a wide range of approaches to the academic study of law - including analysis of the creation and application of legal rules, the impact of law on individuals, organisations and society, the theoretical underpinnings of the concept of law, and the moral and political values expressed in law and legal processes.

The LLB Law programme provides a supportive environment in which students take responsibility for their own learning and aim to become effective life-long learners, with opportunities to review and reflect upon their academic and personal achievements through personal development planning.  "

aims: The Birmingham Award with Distinction / The Birmingham Dubai Award with Distinction is a co-curricular programme that students undertake alongside their degree to develop, recognise, and articulate the attributes that they have developed at Birmingham, in preparation for the graduate recruitment and development processes.

The programme offers a flexible approach to skill development through the formal recognition of both on-and off campus extra-curricular activities, including those from all Colleges, Professional Services, and the Guild of Students.

This provision includes quality-assured structured teaching sessions that allow a learner to explore and develop a deeper understanding of a skill area through classroom-based teaching sessions, and digital education materials, co-created with employer partners.

Each activity recognised by The Birmingham Award will be required to identify the responsibilities of the role/activity and identify between one and four of the institutional Graduate Attributes that a student can develop as a result of engaging. A student will be required to participate in four activities, and for each activity, will need to identify an achievement or career progression goal from engagement, to be eligible to complete the award.

All students are required to complete a compulsory educational programme and associated summative assessments designed to prepare a learner for the graduate recruitment and development process. Each student receives personalised feedback on their assessment to ensure the transformative approach to the curriculum.

data.progTitle: MSc AI and Government Part-time.
data.shortTitle: MSc AI and Government PT
aims: The MSc in AI and Government provides a unique interdisciplinary learning experience at the intersection of technology and public policy. This innovative programme equips students with technical competencies in artificial intelligence alongside contextual understanding of the complexities of government.

Through rigorous training in machine learning, algorithms, programming, statistics, and governance, students gain hard skills to lead development of impactful AI systems. However, the public sector context poses distinct challenges compared to commercial settings. Modules delivered by experts in political science and public administration build awareness of additional considerations around privacy, accountability, stakeholder dynamics, and the political and contested nature of working in the public sector that shape responsible AI adoption and deployment.

The modules introduce the transformative potential alongside heightened risks of these rapidly advancing technologies in the policy sphere. Hands-on projects facilitate learning to address real-world implementation barriers - from procurement to change management - to successfully and ethically embed AI within public organisations. This experiential approach prepares students to drive strategic adoption in complex government environments.

With its blend of technical depth and public sector insight, the programme develops highly skilled professionals ready to pioneer the ethical and effective integration of AI capabilities to enhance governance, deliver public value, and further the public interest. Graduates will lead the responsible transformation of policymaking, service delivery, and regulation in the 21st century.

The key differentiators of the programme are the interdisciplinary nature integrating technical and social science learning, tailored experiential projects applying AI to real public sector contexts, and focus on practical implementation challenges unique to embedding such technologies in government. The key value propositions centre around gaining interdisciplinary expertise tailored to public sector applications, hands-on experiential learning and connections, specialised skills to lead impactful and responsible AI adoption in government and joining a cutting-edge research community focused on the intersection of AI, governance, and policy.

data.progTitle: MSc Interdisciplinary Sport and Exercise Sciences Full-time
data.shortTitle: MSc Interdis Sport & Ex Sci FT
aims: The MSc Interdisciplinary Sport and Exercise Sciences aims to develop students who can interrogate and apply their knowledge and understanding of sport and exercise sciences in an interdisciplinary way.  Through the programme students will gain skills and experience valuable to those interested in careers as a sport or exercise scientist in a high-performance, clinical or community setting. The programme embraces our three key research themes:
1. Sport Participation to Performance
2. Exercise and Health
3. Rehabilitation and motor control

This interdisciplinary programme aims to explore questions of sport and performance and the role of exercise in promoting and maintaining health throughout the lifespan. It will also consider the role of rehabilitation in each of these areas.

Drawing together master's level modules from across the school the programme provides students with a unique opportunity to study in many areas from both scientific and applied perspectives. Topics included are physiology, biochemistry, psychology, rehabilitation and motor control, with the option to take modules in complementary topics such as physical education, coaching, and sociology.  Alongside this the Schools strength in research introduces students to the interdisciplinary nature of both research and practice in the sport and exercise sciences. This interdisciplinarity is fostered through students developing interdisciplinary research skills in the research training modules.

All students carry out an independent research project in a discipline within the programme in which they will address a research question using the interdisciplinary skills that they have developed. The project will also allow them develop skills in project management.
Research projects can be undertaken in an academic or industrial environment.

outcome: 1. Integrative system function / homeostatic mechanisms in response to: stress, injury, exercise, dehydration, temperature fluctuation, fatigue, restricted food intake.
2. The ability of the human body to adapt to exercise, diet, injury and disease.
3. The relationship between different areas of research and adopting an interdisciplinary approach to research techniques and/or research impact.
4. The processes involved in developing a research question, identifying an appropriate design to answer the question.
5. The application of sport, exercise and rehabilitation sciences to work in a variety of settings; both clinical and non-clinical work based environments.
learning: An appropriate mixture of face to face on campus delivery supported by online learning will be used to provide students with opportunities to meet the learning outcomes through the following approaches:

3. Lectures, practicals, seminars and tutorials, independent study, and research projects.
4. Lectures, computer clusters, and seminars on research design and methodology; supervised research projects
5. Lectures, practicals, demonstrations, practical experience, supervised research project

aims: The MSc Global Health System Leadership is aimed at medical and healthcare professionals and policy makers from a variety of non/clinical backgrounds. It is open to all from across the globe but will have a particular focus on those working in the Emirates and neighbouring region. The Eastern Mediterranean Region constitutes 22 countries with diverse situations, many facing conflict and instability and double burden of disease. Additional challenges include climate change, global health security and limitations on public health capacity, which has been magnified during the COVID 19 pandemic. Building a resilient health workforce and systems to advance universal health coverage (UHC) and ensure health security in the Eastern Mediterranean region (EMR) is a top priority.

The MSc Global Health System Leadership works to support health policy development, deliver excellent teaching and put policy into practice by expanding and transforming the health and social care organisation and health workforce within the EMR. Acquiring the knowledge, skills and competencies that speak to the identified nine regional essential public health functions needed to achieve universal health coverage through building resilient health systems and workforce and focusses on extending capabilities in the six global core competencies for UHC. This programme would facilitate the development of knowledge, skills and professional behaviours across these domains through coherent study at Masters Level.

The programme will be attractive to international applicants as there are few opportunities in the Middle East to undertake programmes designed to foster the development of health system and policy experts that are fit-for-purpose and fit-for-practice practitioners to become team leaders, managers, researchers and/or experts. Increasingly there is an expectation from employers that those in middle and senior positions have acquired the attributes inherent in postgraduate study and can demonstrate this through problem solving, supporting, and facilitating other members of the multidisciplinary team and through their leadership in work environments. The modules embedded in the programme structure focus on Global Health Leadership and Management; Global Health Systems and Policy; Strategic Planning; Global Health Economics; Emergency Preparedness Response and Resilience; and Implementation Science.

outcome: Critically analyse and evaluate health systems and policies using theoretical and comparative approaches across different complex, stable and fragile conflict-affected vulnerable settings (FCV), cultures and countries.

Theories, foundational concepts, and context in leadership and management of self, teams, and the organization including concepts of role, power, authority, change and resilience of leaders and managers to develop the knowledge and understanding needed to appraise and evaluate approaches within health systems, complex adaptive systems, and values-based leadership.

Systematic approach to the study of theory and practice of implementation science to recognise, understand and address health system and implementation bottlenecks, identifying, planning, managing and evaluating optimal implementation options for a given setting to improve health system.

Systematic understanding of the basic principles and theories of strategic planning, implementation, monitoring and evaluation, conflict resolution, priority setting and resource mobilisation in relation to health policy and health system strategy and plan.
Comparative approach to the study of different health economic theories, tools, foundational concepts and approaches to critically evaluate the impact on global health system.

Develop an integrated, theoretical and practical knowledge of Health Emergency Preparedness Response and Resilience (EPRR) and to develop the capacity to apply this knowledge in the field of global health system while considering the intersection of health security, primary health care and health promotion, and interface with multiple non-health sectors and stakeholders at national, regional and global levels.
How to meaningfully apply evidence to global health system, policy and leadership.

data.progTitle: MSc AI and Sustainable Development Part-time.
data.shortTitle: MSc AI & Sustain Dev PT
aims: The MSc in AI and Sustainable Development provides interdisciplinary education at the nexus of technology, sustainability, and international development. This innovative programme equips students with technical competencies in artificial intelligence complemented by contextual understanding of deploying such technologies to advance sustainability and development globally.

Through rigorous training, students gain data science and programming skills tailored to real-world challenges constrained by limited data, inadequate infrastructure, and under-resourced environments across the Global South. Coursework delivered by experts in development and sustainability policy, and domain areas builds nuanced appreciation of on-the-ground realities, priorities of marginalised communities, and complex systems interlinkages.

Experiential learning facilitates developing context-specific AI solutions balancing cutting-edge innovation with sustainability, inclusivity, participatory design, and human-centric principles. Graduates lead transformative yet responsible applications of AI furthering poverty alleviation, climate resilience, sustainable production, environmental protection, and climate justice. They pioneer approaches leveraging AI to accelerate decarbonisation, renewable energy, conservation, and regenerative economies while preventing unintended consequences.

With technical expertise coupled with experiential insights, students emerge poised to unlock AI's potential while centring local perspectives and holistic notions of collective wellbeing. They lead sustainable technological change uplifting vulnerable populations and restoring balance across environmental, social, and economic dimensions regionally and worldwide. The programme develops professionals with interdisciplinary mindsets ready to meet interconnected development challenges in the 21st century.

The key differentiators of the programme are the interdisciplinarity, grounded hands-on projects, and focus on responsible and inclusive AI deployment in underserved regions to maximise social, economic, and environmental benefits globally. The key value propositions focus on gaining interdisciplinary expertise grounded in real-world contexts, connections to drive social impact, specialised skills to advance sustainable development through AI globally, and joining a community of changemakers pursuing social justice worldwide.

aims: The MSc Marketing aims to provide students with a solid foundation in marketing theory and ever-evolving issues in marketing practice. The proposed programme seeks to develop graduates with high standards of knowledge of the principles, theoretical concepts and practice of marketing, giving them the opportunity to choose among digital, international or responsible marketing pathways. The goal is to enable students to develop subject-specific expertise coupled with the critical, analytical, communication and ethical capabilities required for a successful marketing career in today's marketplace.

The core content of the programme provides students with the frameworks, theories and concepts necessary to understand the fundamentals of marketing activity.  Modules will cover marketing strategy, planning and management as well as introducing different perspectives and approaches to the understanding of consumer insights.  They will also be introduced to a range of approaches and techniques to market research.  Students will also be able to select from a range of options that will enable them to explore more specialised elements of marketing activity.  For example, they may elect to study marketing communications or services and retail marketing.  In the second semester of the programme, students will be able to choose to focus in detail on one element of contemporary marketing practice, namely digital marketing, international marketing, or responsible marketing.

Alongside the knowledge in marketing, students in this programme will benefit from the Birmingham Business School Future Ready Graduate Framework, in which each taught module is supported by academics, careers development and student experience team to develop transferable skills such as agile mind-set, resilience and personal effectiveness. The programme will help students develop the theoretical and practical skills necessary for a successful marketing career. These skills include critical analytical capabilities, problem solving, critiquing literature and evaluating information sources. Further, they will develop their communication skills, both written and oral, and will have many opportunities to practice them by using IT and organising group and teamwork activities.

The programme will be taught in four 4 teaching blocks. Each block is 6 weeks long and there will be two (2) teaching blocks in Semester one (1), followed by another two (2) teaching blocks in Semester two (2). Therefore, in Semester 1A students will have only one core module to attend, and the programme aims to enhance those first 6 weeks with the critical skills for their success in the programme and future career, as per the Birmingham Business School Future Ready Graduate Framework.
Skills development will also be part of the module delivery in semesters 1B, 2A and 2B, but with a lighter workload for students in order to deliver a balanced student experience.

The MSc Marketing programme will help students develop the theoretical and practical skills necessary for a successful marketing career. These skills include critical analytical capabilities, problem solving, critiquing literature and evaluating information sources. Further, they will develop their communication skills, both written and oral, and will have many opportunities to practice them by using IT and organising group and teamwork activities. They will also gain experience of project work and develop the understanding required to manage marketing research projects through a range of modules, and diverse and inclusive modes of assessment.

2) Evaluate the role and impact of marketing on individuals and society from a range of different perspectives (e.g.: social, cultural, ethical, commercial, environmental) to enable an understanding of what might comprise responsible marketing practice.

4) Develop alternative and creative responses to current challenges facing marketers by synthesising information from a wide range of sources.
5) Critique marketing theory and practice through understanding and application of differing viewpoints, ideas and concepts.
