data.progTitle: MSc Sustainable Energy Systems Full-time
data.shortTitle: MSc Sust Ener Syst (Bham+) FT
aims: The joint MSc in Sustainable Energy Systems takes an interdisciplinary approach with a focus on energy systems and technologies deployment for a sustainable future. Students will be encouraged to consider technology development, engineering, economic, societal, environmental and policy aspects in the context of net zero targets.

Students will learn about the fundamental principles behind the current sustainable energy systems, including fuel cells and hydrogen, energy storage, solar and nuclear energy; and the changes required to meet the energy sustainability targets of the future. They will also have the opportunity to learn about data analysis and numerical modelling, smart power grids, data and digitalisation and policy aspects. The course content will be delivered by research staff who have backgrounds in academia, industry and policy.

Undertaking a substantial individual project with internationally-recognised research groups at both the University of Birmingham and IIT Madras, will give students the opportunity to apply their knowledge to provide solutions to the global energy crisis and address climate change.

Students will be able to select from two programme options when they apply. Both programmes begin with six months at IIT Madras. Then, the Birmingham majority option sees students spend 12 months at the University of Birmingham for the remainder of the taught programme and to conduct a programme of research over the summer. The IIT majority option has students spending six months in Birmingham before returning to IIT Madras to complete the research project and undertake the last part of the taught programme.
Graduates will have specialist, advanced skills and be well prepared for a wealth of jobs including:
Energy data analyst
Whole energy systems analyst
Net-zero consultant
Energy consultant
Sustainability and climate change officer
Energy systems innovation officer
Energy systems retrofitting specialist
Energy Engineer
Applied Scientist
The University of Birmingham has a Careers Network which students can access while studying. An expert team offers advice, mentoring and support with CVs and job applications.

IIT Madras has robust industry connections which make it a highly sought-after destination for recruitment, providing students with ample opportunities to participate in the institute's placement season.

outcome: 1. The major topics, facts and issues related to global energy demand and utilisation, key energy production, storage, transmission and utilisation technologies, key energy economics, environmental and policy issues, and their interdisciplinary nature in informing local, national and global energy systems. (MSc, PGDip)

2. The underlying scientific principles and methodologies for quantitative analysis and evaluation of the above aspects as part of complex energy systems, including sustainability aspects over their life cycle. (MSc, PGDip)
3. The application of quantitative analysis and evaluation methods for the solution of typical, practical energy technology and systems problems. (MSc, PGDip)

4. Research techniques which might include information retrieval, experiment and data analysis, modelling, economic and environmental impact assessment, and ethical aspects of research, as required generating an independent piece of research, and preparing it for publication. (MSc)
5. Management and communication skills, including problem definition, project design, decision processes, negotiation, written and oral reports, scientific publications. (MSc)
learning: 1-3: Acquisition through a combination of formal classroom based teaching, practical classes, tutorials and seminars, in foundation courses.

This new role is seen to be important in pioneering the shift of work, traditionally done only by doctors, to new, non-medically trained grades of staff. It also addresses the current workforce planning problems in anaesthesia.
In detail the aims of the programme are to develop:
a `practitioner? role that enables the anaesthesia team to have more staff working in different ways under the supervision of the medically qualified anaesthetist.
a cadre of non-medical practitioners who are motivated and competent to maintain patient safety, quality of care and outcomes.

practitioners who are clear about the limits of their role, can present it transparently to and can gain and maintain the confidence of, the public and those who manage, fund and work in the health service.
professionals who have the motivation and intellectual capacity to make effective use of continuing education throughout their careers.

aims: Birmingham Business School aims to deliver a learning that is relevant to our executive MBA student's day-to-day work, under the ethos of transforming knowledge from all core business disciplines into practice and new behaviours.
This programme aims to develop responsible, reflective, and resilient business leaders for the promotion of sustainable futures who by the end of the programme will be able to:

1. Integrate and apply critical knowledge and competencies and develop effective governance structures and partnerships to lead, manage and respond to local, regional, and global challenges in a responsible and sustainable way.
2. Demonstrate the skills required for evidence-informed and culturally sensitive and contextual decision making in the changing world of work and business.
3. Continuously broaden their own mindset to sustainably innovate and perform effectively in complex, uncertain and changing business environments.
4. Lead and manage purposefully and inclusively within their organisation and in their interactions with a diverse set of external stakeholders.
5. Demonstrate a creative and entrepreneurial mindset for the development of a sustainable future.
6. Apply relevant knowledge to inspire future organisational strategies.
7. Continuously adapt and develop professionally.

Aiming to deliver an integrative learning experience and the opportunity for our students to focus on their own development in a purposeful way through three elements of learning that makes this programme distinctive.

The first element is the Purposeful Leader module. This module will provide an opportunity for our students to focus on their personal and professional development and to support them with the objectives they have for their career beyond the executive MBA. Students will have the opportunity to reflect on their career ambitions and discuss how those ambitions will inform the choice of final project. In this exercise students will be nurtured to choose a final project which suits their values and career aspirations.

The second distinctive element of learning is the integrative nature of the Global Perspectives on Responsible Business module. This module combines applied learning with values and principles of responsible business and creates and opportunity for a no-boundaries problem assessment and solving approach to develop responsible and sustainable solutions to business issues.

The third distinctive element is the exciting avenues that elective* modules open to our students. As part of the programme students will choose four (4) optional modules from a variety of subjects, types of modules and locations (subject to availability and additional requirements). When choosing electives, students can specialise their degree. The specialisations available are Innovation & Business Transformation, Marketing, and International Business & Strategy.

Through the learning journey we expect that our executive MBA students will develop a range of skills such as analytical skills relevant for business decision making negotiation, communications, leadership, digital skills, interpersonal skills, and stakeholders? management skills.

Finally, aiming to provide our graduates with tangible networking and lifelong learning opportunities, our alumni network will offer opportunities to stay connected with the school and remain at the forefront of business practice and knowledge, for example by being invited to:
join the MBA a regular roundtable discussions and networking opportunities.
join one of the standard optional modules in their MBA programme up to three years after your graduation to promote alumni's continuous development
mentor incoming students, to expand their network and enhance the relationship between academic and business.

aims: The Masters in Mental Health in Edgbaston along with components from a suite of other postgraduate psychology programmes are being brought together with the specific aim of delivering excellence in clinical applications of psychology at MSc level in Dubai and the UAE. This programme would represent the only offering in Dubai meeting the educational component requirements to pursue further professional training aligned with licensing as a clinical psychologist in the UAE, representing a unique and distinct market opportunity (Subsequent supervised practice and exams are required for licensure).
We will aim to initially offer this programme on a full-time basis.
The specific aims of the Masters are:
- To deliver an internationally excellent interdisciplinary Masters level qualification in Mental Health, with a focus on clinical applications of psychology.
- To enhance the skills of the UAE workforce in relation to Mental Health and clinical psychology.
- To integrate the latest Mental Health research into teaching and practice with sufficient and appropriate cultural nuance and contextualisation to the UAE.

- To build an extended alumni faculty of clinicians, public sector staff, researchers, and business and industry partners who are committed to developing future initiatives to support mental health and wellbeing across sectors.

Subsequent supervised practice and exams are required for licensure. As such the university bears no responsibility for the successful licensure of graduating candidates. However, we anticipate that the placement programme in year two will provide candidates an appropriate springboard for this process.

The only analogous programme (the UAE University) provides no research training or research project as part of the compulsory suite of learning and outcomes, additionally, candidates are responsible for developing their own 2 x 12-week clinical placements. The result, based on the availability of competitive programmes and a lack of compulsory research training is a significant knowledge, skill, and competency gap with industry, and a lack of research/evidence-basis to practice and service development. This provision aims to create a new benchmark by which clinical programmes will be assessed, with a focus on the scientific practitioner, clinical excellence, a competency-based framework applied to rigorous and quality-controlled placements of an extensive enough period to represent transformational learning, and excellence in research as an imperative to service development, policy development, and evidence-based practice.
Areas of work include government and private clinical practice, policy development, evaluation, research, and academia.
Rationale for development
The Masters in Mental Health (clinical) is responding to five key market drivers:
? The rising public awareness of mental health, and the increasing demand on public and private services to respond to public demand and mental illness
? The call to skill up the national workforce in relation to people's mental health.
? The increasing awareness of employers of their responsibilities in relation to Workplace Wellbeing and promoting workplace mental health.

? The increased significance that the Mental Health research agenda is receiving in the UAE and internationally, and the need to train the next generation of Mental Health practitioners and researchers and to retain clinical staff in the workforce
? To build capacity in interdisciplinary mental health research.

data.shortTitle: BSc Biotechnology FT
aims: Biotechnology is an interdisciplinary field spanning the biosciences and is going to play a key role in responding to many global issues. It has been at the forefront of some of the most ground-breaking discoveries and innovations in recent years. From developing novel therapies for diseases to designing genetically modified organisms with enhanced traits; and continues to push the boundaries of what is possible in science and medicine. Key disciplines linked to biotechnology include genetics, cell biology, plants sciences, chemistry and chemical engineering. Advances in biotechnology play an important role in shaping various industries and improving the overall quality of life. Biotechnology graduates will benefit from a wide and diverse range of careers and opportunities.

With a growing global population, ensuring food security and sustainable agricultural practices is, and will continue to be, crucial. Although controversial, biotechnology is important for agricultural sustainability with a key role in developing genetically modified crops that are resistant to pests, droughts, and diseases, thereby increasing yield and reducing the environmental impact of farming.

Biotechnology contributes to environmental conservation by offering solutions to pollution, waste management, and the development of renewable energy sources. Biotechnology graduates will contribute to the creation of cleaner and more sustainable technologies.

Biotechnology has and will continue to be a key discipline in the healthcare revolution by enabling the development of precision medicine, gene therapies, and advanced diagnostic tools. Biotechnology undergraduates will develop the knowledge and skills to allow them to contribute to the development of new treatments and technologies within a healthcare setting.

Industries such as pharmaceuticals, biofuels, and bioplastics rely on biotechnological processes to manufacture products efficiently and sustainably. Graduates with a biotechnology degree can work in a variety of sectors and contribute to the development of greener and more efficient industrial processes.

The proposed biotechnology programme will provide students with a diverse skill set that includes biology, chemistry, genetics, microbiology, bioinformatics, and possible engineering. This interdisciplinary approach will develop and enhance problem-solving abilities of our students and prepare graduates to tackle complex challenges from multiple angles. In addition, biotechnology involves discussions about the ethical implications of certain technologies, such as gene editing and cloning and therefore students will be exposed to these ethical discussions, preparing them to navigate complex ethical dilemmas in their future career.

Both the BSc and MSci programme will provide the students with the opportunity to develop their research expertise during the research project and for professional placement students in an industrial setting.

Biotechnology has a global impact, addressing challenges that affect people's lives worldwide, such as disease outbreaks, environmental degradation, and food shortages. Biotechnology graduates will contribute to solving these global issues. Many breakthroughs in biotechnology have led to the creation of successful start-up companies. With the right knowledge and skills, graduates can become entrepreneurs and drive innovation in the biotech industry.

aims: The programme in BA Cultural and Creative Industries aims to equip students with the knowledge and skills to develop and sustain meaningful careers in the global cultural and creative industries. The course offers a unique blend of the study of the cultural and creative industries in terms of investigating their ecologies, current trends, policy frameworks, regulation, technologies, and business models, with creative and artistic opportunities that will prepare graduates for future employment as creative and cultural leaders and visionaries, artistic/creative directors, educators, facilitators, and producers.

This industry- focused and applied programme draws on research and practice-led expertise in theatre, performance, film, creative writing, arts and cultural policy, visual arts, curation, production, and digital media, as well as the legal, business, leadership, and management aspects of these industries. Modules blend theoretical study with real-world case studies, examples, and assessments to prepare graduates for future employment as well-prepared, adaptable, resilient and innovative leaders in this sector. Students also have opportunities through the programme to continue to develop aspects of their own creative practice, ensuring an understanding of the demands of producing cultural work and an ability to realise and deliver a variety of creative projects.

Students will have opportunities to network and undertake work placements to foster their professional development through the extensive connections that the College and School have with cultural partners in the region and beyond. Recognising the vital role of entrepreneurship and innovation in the sector, graduates will develop multidisciplinary skills and build digital literacy to thrive in the rapidly evolving creative and cultural landscape. Students will also explore the social and ethical implications of their work, learning to create, disseminate and promote content that is socially responsible and culturally sensitive. Finally, the programme aims to prepare students for global careers by exposing them to international perspectives and practices within the cultural and creative industries.

Graduates of this program will possess a diverse set of transferable and industry specific skills, providing them with the attributes and knowledge to be dynamic and adaptable leaders, producers, directors, executives, researchers, educators, and imagineers in the cultural and creative industries.
For semester/year abroad only:

Study abroad will provide students with the opportunity to immerse themselves in the society and culture of a foreign country while gaining experience of a different academic environment and way of teaching. The year abroad also provides an opportunity for students to improve their existing language proficiency (where applicable) as well as enhancing their organisation and communication skills and their employability through a proven ability to succeed in a foreign setting.

data.progTitle: MSc AI and Government Full-time
data.shortTitle: MSc AI and Government FT
aims: The MSc in AI and Government provides a unique interdisciplinary learning experience at the intersection of technology and public policy. This innovative programme equips students with technical competencies in artificial intelligence alongside contextual understanding of the complexities of government.

Through rigorous training in machine learning, algorithms, programming, statistics, and governance, students gain hard skills to lead development of impactful AI systems. However, the public sector context poses distinct challenges compared to commercial settings. Modules delivered by experts in political science and public administration build awareness of additional considerations around privacy, accountability, stakeholder dynamics, and the political and contested nature of working in the public sector that shape responsible AI adoption and deployment.

The modules introduce the transformative potential alongside heightened risks of these rapidly advancing technologies in the policy sphere. Hands-on projects facilitate learning to address real-world implementation barriers - from procurement to change management - to successfully and ethically embed AI within public organisations. This experiential approach prepares students to drive strategic adoption in complex government environments.

With its blend of technical depth and public sector insight, the programme develops highly skilled professionals ready to pioneer the ethical and effective integration of AI capabilities to enhance governance, deliver public value, and further the public interest. Graduates will lead the responsible transformation of policymaking, service delivery, and regulation in the 21st century.

The key differentiators of the programme are the interdisciplinary nature integrating technical and social science learning, tailored experiential projects applying AI to real public sector contexts, and focus on practical implementation challenges unique to embedding such technologies in government. The key value propositions centre around gaining interdisciplinary expertise tailored to public sector applications, hands-on experiential learning and connections, specialised skills to lead impactful and responsible AI adoption in government and joining a cutting-edge research community focused on the intersection of AI, governance, and policy.

They will be equipped to work effectively in a professional capacity, for example in industrial design, or research and development.  Graduates should be able to contribute specialist skills to such activities.  They should also have developed the technical, intellectual and transferable skills needed to underpin their education and continuing professional development.

data.longTitle: (Environmental, Social and Governance Law and Policy)
aims: This Taught LLM programme enables graduate students, both from within the European Union and elsewhere, to develop expertise in a variety of subjects in which the School of Law has significant strengths. This taught LLM programme provides a supportive environment in which students take responsibility for their own learning and aim to become effective life long learners.
The programme aims:

1.  to enable students to acquire a systematic understanding of the subjects they study, and a critical awareness of current problems and/or new insights, much of which is at, or informed by, the forefront of the subjects studied.
2. to enable students to acquire a comprehensive understanding of techniques applicable to their own research and advanced scholarship.

3. to encourage students to demonstrate originality in the application of knowledge, together with a practical understanding of how established techniques of research and enquiry are used to create and interpret knowledge in the discipline.
4. to enable students to acquire a conceptual understanding that allows them to evaluate critically current research and advanced scholarship in the discipline.
5 to enable students to develop their skills in research and writing through preparing assessed work and a substantial dissertation written under the supervision of a specialist in the subject.

outcome: 1. A cross-cutting range of fields of law from a list of all modules offered on all LLM programmes and which can cover all or parts of: criminal law and criminal justice, public law, regulation and governance, international and comparative law, commercial law, economic and trade law, environmental and energy law, human rights law, European law, healthcare law and socio-legal studies. (LLM, PGDip, PGCert)
2. The significance of social, political, economic or commercial contexts in which legal rules and principles operate; (LLM, PGDip, PGCert)
3. Comparisons to be drawn between areas of the Law being studied and the Law as it has developed in other jurisdictions where appropriate; (LLM, PGDip, PGCert)

4. The role and importance of persuasive analysis to law and the range of theories that can be applied to offer evidenced conclusions, addressing complex actual or hypothetical problems; and (LLM, PGDip, PGCert)
5. Proposals to reform the areas of Law being studied. (LLM, PGDip, PGCert)
learning: Seminars, lectures and individual assistance with written work
assessment: For all qualifications: Assessed essays; and/or written examinations and/ or presentations; and, for those completing LLM qualification, a dissertation.

outcome: 1. To carry out practical legal research using information technology and paper-based sources (LLM, PGDip, PGCert)
2. To bring together relevant material from primary and secondary sources (LLM, PGDip, PGCert)

3. To produce academic writing to a high standard of scholarship, including writing effectively in the English language and presenting information and ideas in a manner that meets relevant academic conventions (LLM, PGDip, PGCert)

4. To apply legal and related knowledge systematically to complex problems by constructing arguments, recognising potential alternative conclusions and providing supporting reasons (LLM, PGDip, PGCert)
5. To communicate effectively, by giving and receiving information and ideas and modifying responses where appropriate (LLM, PGDip, PGCert)
6. To think critically and creatively about matters covered in the programme, demonstrating a capacity for independent thinking (LLM, PGDip, PGCert)

for those completing LLM qualification, a dissertation.

aims: BA Drama and English Literature is a Single Honours Programme, including study in ancilliary disciplines. It is characterised by a wide study, methodologically and theoretically informed, of the range of literature in the English language from the medieval period to the present, and by the theoretical and practical exploration of a wide range of theatrical and performance styles, from the Renaissance stage to the present. It aims to produce individuals who possess a broad range of knowledge and understanding of English literature and performance; critical skills in the close reading and analysis of texts both literary and non-literary; analytical and practical skills derived from the close analysis of dramatic and performance texts and contexts; organisational and presentational skills, including those derived from work on the production and organisational aspects of theatre and performance; and a developed competence in interpersonal and communicative skills, with particular strengths in collaborative work. The wide range of reasoning, research, independent learning, communication and organisational skills acquired from this programme equips graduates to pursue further study or employment in English, Drama and related disciplines, and is readily transferable to a variety of commercial, cultural and professional careers.
For year abroad only:

Study abroad will provide students with the opportunity to immerse themselves in the society and culture of a foreign country while gaining experience of a different academic environment and way of teaching. The year abroad also provides an opportunity for students to improve their existing language proficiency (where applicable) as well as enhancing their organisation and communication skills and their employability through a proven ability to succeed in a foreign setting.

outcome: A working understanding of the ways in which practical and theoretical work in drama, performance and theatre arts necessarily inform one another.
A substantial number of authors and texts from different periods of literary history.

Different critical and theoretical approaches in the study of literature, language and performance, and of the literary, cultural and historical contexts that inform both the creation, embodiment and reception of texts and performance.
A knowledge of drama and performance in all its aspects.
A working knowledge of the language of theatre and performance practice.
An understanding and appreciation of the theatrical and performative output of different periods and places and an understanding of various critical approaches to theatre and performance.
Thematic and generic links between texts across a wide historical range.
A range of transferable skills which will enable students to work effectively.
Demonstrate the ability to study relevant topics at an international institution and appreciate the difference between study in the UK and overseas.

aims: The BSc Sport, Physical Education and Coaching Science (with Sport Business Management) degree is a unique, dynamic course, designed to produce the best professionals in the fields of sport business and management, education, coaching, sport development, and other physical activity and health industries. This is an interdisciplinary programme which is focused on developing students? theoretical and applied knowledge, as well as expertise and competency in professional practice. Students are engaged in modules that draw from a range of disciplines, including sport pedagogy (teaching and coaching), applied sport sciences (i.e., psychology, physiology, motor control), sport business and management, and research methods. Modules across the school provide the opportunity to study in many areas from both scientific and applied perspectives, and there are increasing opportunities for choosing modules in the second and third year of studies.  To graduate with this bracketed qualification, students need to study all the sport and business management modules run by the School of Sport, Exercise and Rehabilitation Sciences across the three years of study.

aims: 1. This Taught MA in History enables graduate students to develop expertise in a variety of subjects in which the Department of History has significant strengths.(which at present include Medieval Studies; Early Modern History; Global History; US History; Contemporary History; Public History; and Modern British Studies).

2. The programme aims to enable students to acquire a systematic understanding of the subjects they study, and a critical awareness of current problems and/or new insights, much of which is at, or informed by, the forefront of the subjects studied.
3. The programme aims to enable students to acquire a comprehensive understanding of techniques applicable to their own research and advanced scholarship.

4. The programme aims to encourage students to demonstrate originality in the application of knowledge, together with a practical understanding of how established techniques of research and enquiry are used to create and interpret knowledge in the discipline.
5. The programme aims to enable students to acquire a conceptual understanding that allows them to evaluate critically current research and advanced scholarship in the discipline.

6. The programme aims to enable students to develop their skills in research and writing through preparing assessed work and a substantial dissertation written under the supervision of a specialist in the subject.

7. The programme aims to enable students to gain a mixture of generic and discipline-specific skills, providing a solid base both for academic research into History or an allied discipline at doctoral level, and also for the development of a successful professional career, including (but not limited to) fields adjacent to the historical discipline, such as public history and heritage.

8. The programme aims to enable students to specialise in a particular historical pathway, should they wish to, including studying taught modules and writing their dissertation on a topic within the pathway area of specialism.

data.shortTitle: BSc Psychol w Y in Env Sust FT
data.longTitle: Psychology with Year in Environmental Sustainability
aims: Understanding climate and environmental change, how we address its causes, how we live with and respond to its impacts, and how we find sustainable solutions to our use of Earth's resources and impacts of planetary systems, is one of the most pressing issues facing humanity. This one-year programme aims to introduce environmentally motivated students studying in a range of disciplines to the core concepts of environmental change and sustainability, from the perspective of planetary processes and environments impacts, and in terms of developing sustainable solutions to present-day challenges. In an increasingly globalised world, it is of paramount importance that we are able to develop sustainable and interdisciplinary approaches across management of energy, natural resources, food security, biodiversity, ecology, and natural hazards.

Tackling themes across environmental sustainability requires a broad and interdisciplinary approach, and a working knowledge of Earth and Environmental processes and the intersection of human pressures on ecological systems. This one year of study meets this need by providing students with a broad foundation in Earth and Environmental Science and Biosciences, giving the student a working introduction to sustainability challenges alongside a range of transferable cross-disciplinary skills that will support students? skills and careers irrespective of discipline.  The constituent modules introduce the necessary understanding and skills to address the challenges posed by global environmental change and aim to take an interdisciplinary and practical approach.

Graduates who have added this additional year to their existing programme will enter their final year with a different perspective on their core studies and will be equipped for a wider range of graduate employment.

aims: To provide access to BSc Honours level education in Biology for higher quality students of which the majority are traditionally post A-level; To develop a broad appreciation in UG students of the scope of modern biology, encompassing levels of biological organisation from molecules to ecosystems, and major groups of organisms; To maximise flexibility and opportunities for choice of modules and degree programmes so that UG students develop from an initial understanding of a broad core of biological sciences and maintain that breadth of study throughout the programme or move towards increasing specialisation; To provide students with the possibility of experiencing current research, its methodology and significance; To encourage students to progress from dependent to independent learners and critical thinkers; To stimulate students to acquire a long-term interest in, and enthusiasm for, biology and scientific scholarship; To enable students to move into a range of biological careers, either immediately after graduation or following further specialist training; To encourage the development of transferable skills (e.g. intellectual, numerical, analytical, communication) enabling students to move into diverse contemporary occupations;  To provide pastoral support and guidance to enable students to maximise their achievements within their degree programme. optional.ruleText: The core Purposeful Leader module together with one of the 40 credits modules involves student research and make up 60 credits of independent learning based on student research within the MBA Programme. Students must choose ONE from the following modules. Students who choose optional modules with the aim of being awarded an MBA in a business specialism must also choose a topic for their project which is within that business specialism. To take the Entrepreneurial Project, students must have previously taken Entrepreneurship and Innovation.

Students must choose an additional 40 credits in total. At least one of the optional modules must be in students? home location (Exec-UK). The other three options they can choose in any of the locations of the part-time programmes as part of the student mobility available to them, such as Dubai, Singapore and Online MBA, as well as in their home programme in the UK. Amongst the optional modules, students can choose up to a maximum of one module from the Clinical Leadership and/or Engineering Leadership specialist programmes, and those modules have further entry criteria, which students will need to meet to enrol in any of those modules. Please note, student mobility may lead to a longer programme duration due to timetabling of PT programmes and is subject to visa regulations, which are not managed by the MBA programme. When choosing the elective modules, students can also choose a specialism. There are three specialisms students can choose from: Marketing; International Business & Strategy; and Innovation & Business Transformation. These require a specific combination of optional modules. The requirements for these three pathways are outlined below. Students are able to choose ONE module from the list of immersive modules.

Students who wish to be awarded the Marketing pathway (exit qualification: MBA (Marketing) must choose 40 credits of optional modules, at least two of which must include Digital Marketing, Corporate Communication and Reputation Management, Services Marketing, and/or Global Marketing Consultancy: International Residential (Immersive module). data.progTitle: BSc Mathematical Economics and Statistics with Placement Year Full-time
data.shortTitle: BSc Math Econ + Stat w Plac Ye
data.longTitle: Mathematical Economics and Statistics with Placement Year
aims: This programme provides students with an understanding of economic concepts, principles and tools, with a particular focus on mathematical and statistical methods. The programme aims to stimulate students intellectually through the study of economics and to lead them to appreciate its application to a range of problems and its relevance in a variety of contexts. Students should receive a firm foundation of knowledge about the workings of economic systems and develop the relevant skills for the constructive use of that knowledge in a range of settings.

The first year of the programme provides a foundation in economics and a rigorous grounding in mathematics and statistics. The second year develops a core of Microeconomics, Macroeconomics and Econometrics, alongside more specialised policy-based and theoretical modules. In the final year of the programme, there is more advanced coverage of econometrics and mathematical economics together with increased flexibility to specialise in a number of theoretical and policy-oriented fields.

The programme provides students with advanced mathematical and technical skills that are applicable to the study of Economics and transferable to other areas, including analytical skills and an ability to develop simplifying frameworks for studying the real world. On graduating, students will be well prepared to work in a range of graduate careers, for example in banking, finance or general management careers, or to progress to Masters-level study in Economics.

outcome: Economic concepts and principles addressing microeconomic issues, such as consumption, production, markets and market failure, economic welfare, and macroeconomic issues, such as employment, national income, the balance of payments, economic growth, business cycles, and the role of the financial system in the economy.

Relevant advanced quantitative methods and tools for data analysis including appropriate mathematical and statistical methods, computational techniques and econometrics, taking into account compliance with data usage regulations.

Relevant theoretical, model-based and empirical analytical tools, and different methodological approaches to the analysis of economic policy and applications of relevant economic principles and reasoning.
Application of economic principles, their mathematical formulation, and the statistical means by which theories and propositions can be evaluated to a variety of topics.
Relevant verbal, graphical, mathematical and econometric representations and communication of economic ideas and analysis, in various relevant media.

data.shortTitle: MA First World War Studies PT
aims: The educational aim of this programme is to provide students with a knowledge and understanding of the challenges posed by the First World War to states to militaries and to societies and of the evolving ways in which these challenges were met. Some parts of the course focus more on Britain but there are also ample opportunities to see the war from a truly transnational perspective, involving Europe and the wider world. One module focuses explicitly on the war as a global event.  The programme will equip students with the research skills to read and assess relevant primary sources and place them in a wider historical context pertaining to both long established debates around military strategy and diplomacy, and more recent ones taking in culture, society, Empire, nationhood and indeed the nature of the historical process itself.  And it will provide them with the ability to carry out research and to write it up, showing independence of thought and judgement. The programme also provides a springboard from which any student can proceed to research masters or doctoral level study where appropriate. Most of the taught elements will be delivered at the National Army Museum, London, bringing students closer to materials directly relevant to their field of study. By utilising a part-time Saturday day school model of delivery, the programme looks also seeks to attract a wider and more diverse range of students than would be possible with a standard Monday-Friday schedule.

aims: The MSc Mental Health Distance Learning is an online only academic postgraduate degree (and associated postgraduate qualifications) focused on interdisciplinary approaches to mental health research and theory. Aligned with the research excellence and specialisms of the Institute for Mental Health (IMH) by studying the MSc Mental Health Distance Learning you are undertaking an online programme of postgraduate study unique in its focuses on interdisciplinary approaches to mental health and youth mental health.

The MSc Mental Health Distance Learning is responding to four key market drivers: increased public awareness of mental health, calls for increasing knowledge in the youth mental health work force, employer awareness of mental health promotion, and to build capacity for mental health research of an interdisciplinary nature. The MSc Mental Health Distance Learning seeks to provide interdisciplinary and youth mental health relevant knowledge and skills to students from a wide range of international, professional, and career development, arenas through online only provision.
The aims of the MSc Mental Health Distance Learning are:
To deliver an internationally excellent interdisciplinary Master’s level qualification in Mental Health, with a focus on Youth Mental Health through distance learning.

To enhance the knowledge and skills of the global mental health workforce across multiple sectors in relation to Mental Health through full MSc and other post-graduate qualifications (PG Cert, PG Dip) and micro-credential options, delivered through distance learning.
To integrate the latest Mental Health research into distance learning teaching and practice

By studying the MSc Mental Health Distance Learning you will develop transferable skills commensurate with an interdisciplinary MSc programme in a mental health context, including critical evaluation of theoretical and empirical evidence, research design execution and evaluation, data management, writing for different audiences and formation of formal documents (e.g., reports, proposals, etc.), formation of narrative arguments based on appraisal of evidence. You will also develop in depth interdisciplinary academic knowledge of mental health research, practice, and policy. These skills and knowledge will aid in career development in a number of public sector, private sector, charity sector, and research fields of employment, that are relevant to mental health.

aims: The programme aims to provide interdisciplinary postgraduate training in the knowledge and skills needed to address the mitigation and adaptation challenges of climate change, from regional to international scales.
Students will develop a critical understanding of:
? The lines of evidence informing projections of climate impacts, from the global to local scale
? The interplay of meteorology and climate with society in contexts including infrastructure, ecosystems, health
? The challenges of sustainable development within planetary boundaries
? Policy frameworks for mitigating and adapting to climate change, from global to national scales
? Frameworks for leadership and management of change
Students will develop skills in:
? Data processing and statistical methods
? Designing and undertaking independent research
? Critically reviewing lines of evidence for both climate impacts and appropriate adaptation strategies, with consideration of the needs of diverse interested groups
? Communicating climate change challenges, uncertainties, and adaptation options to stakeholders from varied backgrounds
Through optional modules, students will have the opportunity to explore specific topics in further depth, which may include e.g. river management; green infrastructure.
Dissertations include options for both Knowledge Exchange and Placement pathways, allowing opportunities to interact with stakeholders and build industry experience.

After graduation, students are expected to be well-prepared to apply these skills, for example in policy, consultancy or Environment Social Governance (ESG) roles. The course is designed to map to the IEMA Graduate Membership Standard, providing students with an accreditation prioritised in these sectors.

This is an interdisciplinary programme that combines elements of Human Sciences including genetics, sociology, psychology, evolutionary biology, biochemistry, neurosciences and anthropology coupled with understanding the past and ongoing impact of the human race and the human condition on ecosystems and the planet. The aim is to graduate students with a strong sense and understanding of humans and their global impact with a `can do attitude? to the tackling of large scale global and local challenges.

Students will receive broad training in the core elements of Human Sciences from which they can choose to maintain breadth of study or develop in depth expertise in one or more subject areas most suited to their individual interests and aptitudes. Flexibility and choice are maximised by drawing on key strengths across the Schools of Biosciences, Geography, Earth & Environmental Sciences, Psychology, and Sport, Exercise & Rehabilitation Sciences. Students will be given a unique opportunity to explore methods of acquiring, processing, displaying, understanding and communicating of data across the multiple disciplines within these four Schools. Also embedded throughout the programme are opportunities to develop and enhance a range of employability skills, transferable across a diverse range of careers and further study opportunities.

aims: The programme aims to provide interdisciplinary postgraduate training in the knowledge and skills needed to address the mitigation and adaptation challenges of climate change, from regional to international scales.
Students will develop a critical understanding of:
? The lines of evidence informing projections of climate impacts, from the global to local scale
? The interplay of meteorology and climate with society in contexts including infrastructure, ecosystems, health
? The challenges of sustainable development within planetary boundaries
? Policy frameworks for mitigating and adapting to climate change, from global to national scales
? Frameworks for leadership and management of change
Students will develop skills in:
? Data processing and statistical methods
? Designing and undertaking independent research
? Critically reviewing lines of evidence for both climate impacts and appropriate adaptation strategies, with consideration of the needs of diverse interested groups
? Communicating climate change challenges, uncertainties, and adaptation options to stakeholders from varied backgrounds
Through optional modules, students will have the opportunity to explore specific topics in further depth, which may include e.g. river management; green infrastructure.
Dissertations include options for both Knowledge Exchange and Placement pathways, allowing opportunities to interact with stakeholders and build industry experience.

After graduation, students are expected to be well-prepared to apply these skills, for example in policy, consultancy or Environment Social Governance (ESG) roles. The course is designed to map to the IEMA Graduate Membership Standard, providing students with an accreditation prioritised in these sectors.

aims: The programme will:
provide students who are aspiring to more senior roles in healthcare leadership with the theoretical knowledge and practical understanding to help them work more effectively as leaders.
equip students with the professional skills that will be required in a more senior healthcare leadership role, and which is sought after by their employing organisations.
equip students with the theoretical and practical skills to undertake a rigorous and critical evaluation of healthcare leadership.

The programme structure focuses on leadership at three levels - individual, team and organisation – and takes students through a learning journey that focuses on care quality and patient experience, where equality and diversity are proactively implemented.  This is aligned to six leadership objectives:
Understanding how they, as leaders, can make a difference to improving care quality and patient experience
Enabling others to give their best to improve care quality and patient experience
Embedding behaviours that improve care quality and patient experience
Making person centred coordinated care happen
Making decisions based upon the best available evidence to improve care quality and patient experience
Creating value for patients and the public

The programme applies cutting-edge learning methods to maximise learning, blending a flexible state-of-the-art virtual campus with face to face workshops and regional action learning days. This blended learning approach is in keeping with the University’s key teaching and learning approaches and builds upon expertise within the School.

aims: BA Drama and Film is characterised by a wide study, which is methodologically- and theoretically- informed, of Film, ranging across genres, modes and media, combined with the theoretical and practical exploration of a wide range of theatrical and performance styles, from British playwrights and actor training to immersive practices and directing.

Students will develop a deep and rich understanding of the generative, compositional and self-reflective processes involved in creative work in both disciplines, learning practical, technical and industry-specific skills en route. Students will also engage critically with the history and thematic dimensions of both disciplines, encountering a wide range of approaches to Drama and Film in different historical periods. In the third year, students will have the opportunity to take the Professional Skills Module, to undertake a placement or progress their own entrepreneurial project.
The programme aims to produce individuals who possess a broad range of knowledge and understanding of Drama and Film. It will give students the opportunity to:
Develop analytical and practical skills derived from close reading of a wide range of film and performance texts and informed by critical studies
Understand different modes of representation on stage and on film, and how they are socially and politically informed
Gain skills in writing, reasoning, presentation, performance and independent research
Work creatively through film and performance practices to explore a diversity of ways of engaging different audiences
Understand the histories and practices of film-making and performance, underpinned by key theoretical approaches
Develop interpersonal and communication skills, with particular strengths in collaboration and teamwork
Gain an understanding of how to narrate these skills to future employers.

The wide range of reasoning, research, independent learning, communication and creative skills acquired from this programme equips graduates to pursue further study or employment in Drama and Film related disciplines, and is readily transferable to a variety of commercial, cultural and professional careers, including the creative arts, film or media sectors.
For semester/year abroad programmes only:

Study abroad will provide students with the opportunity to immerse themselves in the society and culture of a foreign country while gaining experience of a different academic environment and way of teaching. Study abroad also provides an opportunity for students to improve their existing language proficiency (where applicable) as well as enhancing their organisation and communication skills and their employability through a proven ability to succeed in an unfamiliar setting.
For Year in Civic Leadership only:

The Year in Civic Leadership allows students to put into practice the theoretical knowledge and skills developed during their academic studies, and to critically reflect on this activity, by devising a civic engagement project in collaboration with local community actors. The modules deepen student's appreciation of civic engagement, encouraging them to think about how they can enrich the communities they live and work in.

aims: The MSc Advanced Clinical Practice and MSc Advanced Clinical Practice (Degree Apprenticeship) are aimed at healthcare professionals from a variety of clinical backgrounds with a range of skills who want to develop their research and leadership skills and clinical expertise at master's level. This programme will be of interest to those wishing to work towards advanced levels of practice or those appointed to a ACP trainee post.
There are defined pathways through the programmes to allow ACPs to undertake specific academic modules that enable them to specialise in different areas of practice.

1. The generic MSc Advanced Clinical Practice and the MSc Advanced Clinical Practice (Degree Apprenticeship) have 2 defined pathways to acknowledge the professional specific legislation around Independent Prescribing and specialty requirements:
i. Practice Certificate in Independent Prescribing (IP) pathway
ii. Research and Clinical pathway.

2. The MSc Advanced Clinical Practice (Musculoskeletal Physiotherapy) (Degree Apprentice) pathway is only available for physiotherapists registered with the HCPC with suitable experience in musculoskeletal physiotherapy, as per MACP requirements (see appendix 3).

3. The MSc Advanced Clinical Practice (Advanced Critical Care Practitioner) and MSc Advanced Clinical Practice (Advanced Critical Care Practitioner) (Degree Apprentice) pathways are only available for applicants with a current registration with either the Nursing and Midwifery Council (Part 1 or 2) or The Health and Care Professions Council and three years? post-qualifying experience in intensive care.

4. The MSc Advanced Clinical Practice (Midwifery) and MSc Advanced Clinical Practice (Midwifery) (Degree Apprentice) pathways are only available for registered midwives with suitable post registration experience and a suitable role in practice to support the supervised workbased learning requirements.

All  pathways are mapped to the capabilities for advanced clinical practice in England outlined in the      Multi-professional Framework for Advanced Clinical Practice (2017) reflecting the four pillars of advanced clinical practice:
i. Clinical practice
ii. Leadership and management
iii. Education
iv. Research

In addition, both Degree Apprenticeship programmes have been designed to meet the requirements of the occupational standard for ACP as set by the Institute of Apprenticeships and approved for delivery by the healthcare trailblazer (March 2018): https://www.instituteforapprenticeships.org/apprenticeship- standards/advanced-clinical-practitioner-degree/
Occupational profile:

Advanced Clinical Practitioners are experienced clinicians who demonstrate expertise in their scope of practice. Advanced Clinical Practitioners manage defined episodes of clinical care independently, from beginning to end, providing care and treatment from the time an individual (1) first presents through to the end of the episode, which may include admission, referral or discharge or care at home. They carry out their full range of duties in relation to individuals? physical and mental healthcare and in acute, primary, urgent and emergency settings (including hospitals, general practice, individuals? homes, schools and prisons, and in the public, independent, private and charity sectors). They combine expert clinical skills with research, education and clinical leadership within their scope of practice. Advanced Clinical Practitioners work innovatively on a one-to-one basis with individuals as well as part of a wider team.
They work as part of the wider health and social care team and across traditional professional boundaries in health and social care.

aims: Prevailing healthcare challenges demand innovative and integrative use of diverse technologies to deliver patient-centred care, especially with growing needs of ageing world population. This has led to new trends in health technologies where the objective is to develop connected and intelligent solutions for prevention and personalised healthcare. In moving from the mechanical medical devices to smart electromechanical devices and novel therapeutics, a huge demand in research and development (R&D) in the medical and biotechnology (Med/Bio Tech) industry has resulted in a skill gap over the past few years. There are around 27,000 medical technology companies in Europe, of which 95% are SMEs, which heavily rely on research and innovation. In recent market surveys, there has been 51% increase in R&D jobs, 43% regulatory, 78% business innovation and 23% commercialisation in MedTech industry. In UK alone, over 4,000 businesses employ more than 130,000 health technology professionals, including engineers, scientists, regulatory experts, data experts and management professionals, and more than 575,000 are employed in MedTech sector in Europe. MedTech industry is struggling to recruit new skilled talent with desired skillset to suit to the needs of transforming health technology sector that creates a market for a training and education programme at a higher level than the basic degree.

On the other hand, this new era of technology-led healthcare, brings in challenges of training of healthcare professionals, which is one of the major barriers in adoption of new health technologies. In a study on adoption of new technologies by American Medical Association, it is reported that the physician adoption of technology was facilitated by the availability of resources and training, access to accurate data, positive impact on quality of care, and evidence-base for the tech solution. The way forward to overcome the barriers to adoption of new technologies is to include the healthcare professionals in the health technology innovation and effectively communicate the change. At the same time, young professionals are welcoming the change and are open to understand and get involved in health technology innovation.

Need-led innovation, pioneered by Stanford BioDesign Programme, has been adopted by several organisations globally, including European Institute of Innovation and Technology. The Stanford BioDesign Programme alone has enabled 25 new MedTech start-ups resulting in over $275 million in investment, creation of more than 470 new jobs and improvement of patient outcomes especially where the existing healthcare settings are insufficient. Other similar programmes have been extremely successful in making similar impact and training the students to be more productive and skilful for job market in MedTech and Biotech sector.

The proposed new programme is designed to apply need-led innovation methodology and provide necessary skillset, training, and mentorship to the students to enable innovation as one of the core objectives of the programme. It will increase the postgraduate intake and develop inter-professional learning to prepare the healthcare professionals to embrace the transformations in modern healthcare.

The programme will nourish lean thinking in healthcare professionals and enable inter-disciplinary coordination to understand and adopt new health technologies as well as be an active contributor in the innovation. The programme will host students with basic degrees in health sciences, engineering, life sciences, biotechnology, information technology, data sciences and medicine, providing a unique ecosystem for cross-disciplinary knowledge sharing. It is anticipated that the student cohort will be diverse, which is also important for the programme, therefore the course work is designed to accommodate students with all backgrounds.

aims: History of Art
To provide a programme that allows the history of art to be studied from a range of different perspectives
To maintain an intellectually challenging, coherent and stimulating curriculum
To enhance students' learning experiences by offering modules which are informed and invigorated by the research and publications undertaken by members of staff
To provide a programme of increasing sophistication that enables students to tackle problems of growing complexity.
To instill in students an understanding of works of art seen in the original.
To develop a range of transferable skills in oral and written expression and communication, and in powers of self discipline and organisation.
To maintain a system of pastoral care and monitoring so as to encourage the best performances of our students.
To develop student expertise in the study, analysis and interpretation of visual and moving images in their historical and cultural contexts.

To give students the opportunity to become involved in the theoretical and practical concerns of a working art gallery through a variety of activities, and to engage with both the collection and its staff in a variety of ways.
English Literature

The wide range of reasoning, research, independent learning, communication and organisational skills acquired from this programme equips graduates to pursue further study or employment in English and related disciplines, and is readily transferable to a wide range of commercial, cultural and professional careers.
Programme Aims:
? a wide study, methodologically and theoretically informed, of the range of literature in the English language from the medieval period to the present;

? through study of the range, kinds, structure and character of literature in the English language it aims to produce individuals who possess a broad range of knowledge and understanding of English literature and performance;

? to instil in students critical skills in the close reading and analysis of texts both literary and non-literary; responsiveness to the central role of language in the creation of meaning; rhetorical skills of effective communication and argument, both oral and written;
? to provide students with bibliographic skills appropriate to the discipline;
? to provide students with an understanding of the role of cultural norms in understanding and judgement;
? to provide students with awareness of how different social and cultural contexts affect the nature of language and meaning.
For year abroad programmes only:

The year abroad will provide students with the opportunity to immerse themselves in the society and culture of a foreign country while gaining experience of a different academic environment and way of teaching. The year abroad also provides an opportunity for students to improve their existing language proficiency (where applicable) as well as enhancing their organisation and communication skills and their employability through a proven ability to succeed in a foreign setting.

data.shortTitle: MSc Human Resource Mgt FT
aims: The MSc HRM programme is distinctive in providing students with advanced level intellectual grounding in core knowledge and understanding of people management and the employment relationship in a wider national and global comparative context (notably comparative political economy of work, labour markets, technology, society and culture, the regulation of work, and futures of work). It equips graduates with `big picture? critical thinking skills to become reflective and evidence-led people management practitioners and experts in the world of work. Knowledge of academic theory is used to instil greater understanding of real-life people management practice.

Birmingham Business School is home to one of the strongest research-led teaching groups of HRM, employment relations and organisation studies academics (in the Organisation, Work and Employment group) in the UK. It is also home to the Work Inclusivity Research Centre (WIRC). WIRC academics are committed to the critically engaged study of issues of equality, diversity and inclusion in employment, guided by principles of ethics and social justice, which makes this programme distinctive. This is reflected in a comprehensive MSc HRM programme that in its core modules introduces and further develops the four core pillars of HRM function: resourcing organisations (recruitment & selection), developing organisations (human resource development), reward at work, employment relations.

The School, and the MSc HRM programme, are also distinctive in placing responsible business and good people management at the forefront of teaching and research. As well as providing our graduates with the skills and knowledge to become effective HR practitioners, a key priority is for our graduates to become more ethically aware and responsible organisational citizens, equipped to develop and promote good people management ideas and practices (including, fairness at work; equality, diversity and inclusion; employee voice and influence at work). Students will have the opportunity to investigate these issues during the HRM and Ethics at Work, and Managing Equality and Diversity modules, for example.

The programme also promotes an international comparative focus on HRM and the employment relationship, enabling students to have a better multi-level `big picture? understanding of the world of work. Students will develop greater comparative understanding during the International Perspectives on Employment Relations and International HRM modules, for instance.

data.deliveringInstitution2: National College for Advanced Transport & Infrastructure
aims: Widening participation and addressing the skills gap in this sector above KEY Stage 4 in the West Midlands, are the two aims of the programme. The programme is distinctive in that it is aimed towards students who would not normally qualify for entry to a UoB degree programme. The experience of NCATI in working in further education and with small cohorts of students requiring different study support from those at UoB is used to enable students to make the step up to Higher Education. Students graduating with the Foundation Degree (which is validated by UoB) who pass all modules will be accepted for entry to the third year of one of two BEng/MEng programmes; Civil Engineering or Civil and Railway Engineering. They will graduate from UoB after one year BEng/two years MEng of honours level study. The Foundation Degree is validated under a collaborative provision agreement that ensures a benchmarking of student attainment against UoB assessments and quality assurance in line with UoB processes.

Students will also be encouraged and assisted to find placement opportunities, with guidance as required from UoB under the collaborative provision agreement. The skills gained are aligned with the UKSPEC Learning Outcomes for accredited programmes: the curriculum map and learning outcomes are also aligned with Years 1 and 2 of the equivalent UoB programmes.

The Foundation Degree is a qualification in its own right and students may stop their academic journey after two years at NCATI with FdEng. The programme specification is for the Foundation Degree only. Graduates from the Foundation Degree who do not progress to UoB will be expected to find employment, in transport, information technology, construction sectors; the scheme is intended to impact the local region.

data.shortTitle: MSc(I) Health Data Science FT
aims: This programme provides students with a diversity of skills with hands-on expertise in utilising healthcare data suited to the needs of future health data scientists, enabling them to perform analyses and develop novel tools and methods for this rapidly growing field. It is aimed at students with diverse backgrounds from biomedical/medical domains, including clinical trainees, as well as Computer Sciences, Mathematics and Statistics to conduct their own analyses, and also to create the next generation of cutting-edge health data scientists who will be able to develop new tools and methods matching the latest technological advancements

Students will learn about the breadth of the fields of health data science, from medicine and biology, over ethics and health care systems, to mathematical modelling and computer sciences. They will be able to design, perform and enhance analyses with the appropriate methods and technologies to address practical medical and clinical questions.

This program fits well within the University and College strategies to increase postgraduate programmes that enhance education and research capabilities in the health data and biosciences. Further, playing a role in the creation of the next generation of bioinformaticians will improve the University's standings as a global leader in biomedical research.

data.shortTitle: LLM Int Propery Law (Path) PT
aims: This Taught LLM programme enables graduate students, both from within the European Union and elsewhere, to develop expertise in a variety of subjects in which the School of Law has significant strengths. This taught LLM programme provides a supportive environment in which students take responsibility for their own learning and aim to become effective life long learners.
The programme aims:

1.  to enable students to acquire a systematic understanding of the subjects they study, and a critical awareness of current problems and/or new insights, much of which is at, or informed by, the forefront of the subjects studied.
2. to enable students to acquire a comprehensive understanding of techniques applicable to their own research and advanced scholarship.

3. to encourage students to demonstrate originality in the application of knowledge, together with a practical understanding of how established techniques of research and enquiry are used to create and interpret knowledge in the discipline.
4. to enable students to acquire a conceptual understanding that allows them to evaluate critically current research and advanced scholarship in the discipline.
5 to enable students to develop their skills in research and writing through preparing assessed work and a substantial dissertation written under the supervision of a specialist in the subject.

outcome: 1. A cross-cutting range of fields of law from a list of all modules offered on all LLM programmes and which can cover all or parts of: criminal law and criminal justice, public law, regulation and governance, international and comparative law, commercial law, economic and trade law, environmental and energy law, human rights law, European law, healthcare law and socio-legal studies. (LLM, PGDip, PGCert)
2. The significance of social, political, economic or commercial contexts in which legal rules and principles operate; (LLM, PGDip, PGCert)
3. Comparisons to be drawn between areas of the Law being studied and the Law as it has developed in other jurisdictions where appropriate; (LLM, PGDip, PGCert)

4. The role and importance of persuasive analysis to law and the range of theories that can be applied to offer evidenced conclusions, addressing complex actual or hypothetical problems; and (LLM, PGDip, PGCert)
5. Proposals to reform the areas of Law being studied. (LLM, PGDip, PGCert)
learning: Seminars, lectures and individual assistance with written work
assessment: For all qualifications: Assessed essays; and/or written examinations and/ or presentations; and, for those completing LLM qualification, a dissertation.

data.progTitle: MSc Conflict, Security and Development Part-time.
data.shortTitle: MSc Confli, Securi + Develo PT
aims: This programme recognises the opportunities for educational provision in an area of increasing interest amongst the academic community, namely the links between peace, conflict and development.

Reflects contemporary debates internationally about the nature of peace and conflict in the developing world and the approaches of the international community to support and create peaceful governance in areas of conflict, the programme makes a direct link between academic and practical policy approaches to analysing and recovering from conflicts, with an emphasis on developing countries, and will provide an extensive menu of choices for masters level students. Contemporary debates cover issues as broad as accountability and transparency, corruption, conflict, political settlement, human rights, participation, access to justice, democratisation and security, and will be of interest to individuals already working in development or recent graduates with some work/volunteer experience seeking careers in development or government, or in NGOs related to governance and peace.

This programme provides a framework for exploring academic synergies and for students to undertake genuinely interdisciplinary study. Students leaving this programme will be academically well-trained but also be in a position to undertake careers in conflict analysis, good governance and management in the developing world.

outcome: The dynamics of conflict and post-conflict politics, including the linkages between good governance, state security, state resilience, fragility or collapse and approaches to reconstructing peace following violence
Relevant debates, theories and approaches to development  innovations in theories and practices of good governance and in application to developing and transitional countries.

Design and implementation of post-conflict peacebuilding, security and development strategies, including contemporary debates related to international intervention, local political systems, hybridity and the politics of peacebuilding.
learning: Guided learning through module handbooks, set readings, online exercises, self-directed research through the e-library. Case studies, small group work, Canvas support, audio-visual materials, online discussion, policy document work, practical work.
assessment: Online discussion activities and assignments, peer assessment, learning diaries, assessed essays, dissertation.

outcome: Ability to critically analyse and understand complex conflicts, including capacity to access, interpret and critically analyse material from different sources including policy documents and other publications from governments and international organisations, documents from the internet, and from academic journals

Understanding of the relationships and motivations between actors involved in conflict, fragile states and peacebuilding over time, including political analysis of actors and interest groups engaged in post-conflict environments and fragile states.

Ability to understand and evaluate approaches to post-conflict reconstruction and development and to critically analyse costs and benefits of different external and international intervention strategies in fragile states.

Ability to clearly and concisely argue the case for and against a range of development strategies, including constructing and presenting arguments, clearly analysing data sources and critically evaluating available literature..
Ability to apply and choose appropriate research methods to complex research subjects.
learning: Guided learning through module handbooks, set readings, online exercises, self-directed research through the e-library. Case studies, small group work, Canvas support, audio-visual materials, online discussion, policy document work, practical work [1-5]
All the above, plus IDD's online research methods module and other self-enrolling online research skills courses provided by the UoB. [5]
assessment: Online discussion activities and assignments, peer assessment, learning diaries, assessed essays, dissertation.
