aims: BA Drama and Film is characterised by a wide study, which is methodologically- and theoretically- informed, of Film, ranging across genres, modes and media, combined with the theoretical and practical exploration of a wide range of theatrical and performance styles, from British playwrights and actor training to immersive practices and directing.

Students will develop a deep and rich understanding of the generative, compositional and self-reflective processes involved in creative work in both disciplines, learning practical, technical and industry-specific skills en route. Students will also engage critically with the history and thematic dimensions of both disciplines, encountering a wide range of approaches to Drama and Film in different historical periods. In the third year, students will have the opportunity to take the Professional Skills Module, to undertake a placement or progress their own entrepreneurial project.
The programme aims to produce individuals who possess a broad range of knowledge and understanding of Drama and Film. It will give students the opportunity to:
Develop analytical and practical skills derived from close reading of a wide range of film and performance texts and informed by critical studies
Understand different modes of representation on stage and on film, and how they are socially and politically informed
Gain skills in writing, reasoning, presentation, performance and independent research
Work creatively through film and performance practices to explore a diversity of ways of engaging different audiences
Understand the histories and practices of film-making and performance, underpinned by key theoretical approaches
Develop interpersonal and communication skills, with particular strengths in collaboration and teamwork
Gain an understanding of how to narrate these skills to future employers.

The wide range of reasoning, research, independent learning, communication and creative skills acquired from this programme equips graduates to pursue further study or employment in Drama and Film related disciplines, and is readily transferable to a variety of commercial, cultural and professional careers, including the creative arts, film or media sectors.
For semester/year abroad programmes only:

Study abroad will provide students with the opportunity to immerse themselves in the society and culture of a foreign country while gaining experience of a different academic environment and way of teaching. Study abroad also provides an opportunity for students to improve their existing language proficiency (where applicable) as well as enhancing their organisation and communication skills and their employability through a proven ability to succeed in an unfamiliar setting.
For Year in Civic Leadership only:

The Year in Civic Leadership allows students to put into practice the theoretical knowledge and skills developed during their academic studies, and to critically reflect on this activity, by devising a civic engagement project in collaboration with local community actors. The modules deepen student's appreciation of civic engagement, encouraging them to think about how they can enrich the communities they live and work in.

aims: English Literature

The wide range of reasoning, research, independent learning, communication and organisational skills acquired from this programme equips graduates to pursue further study or employment in English and related disciplines, and is readily transferable to a wide range of commercial, cultural and professional careers.
- a wide study, methodologically and theoretically informed, of the range of literature in the English language from the medieval period to the present;

- through study of the range, kinds, structure and character of literature in the English language it aims to produce individuals who possess a broad range of knowledge and understanding of English literature and performance;

- to instil in students critical skills in the close reading and analysis of texts both literary and non-literary; responsiveness to the central role of language in the creation of meaning; rhetorical skills of effective communication and argument, both oral and written;
- to provide students with bibliographic skills appropriate to the discipline;
- to provide students with an understanding of the role of cultural norms in understanding and judgement;
- to provide students with awareness of how different social and cultural contexts affect the nature of language and meaning.
Philosophy

The programmes aim to provide students with an understanding and appreciation of central areas of philosophy, its methods and history. It aims to engage their interest in and enthusiasm for issues of philosophy and to foster within them the skills distinctive of good philosophy in particular, the abilities to:
- analyse abstract claims and arguments accurately;
- present their own views verbally and in writing, clearly and with supporting argument
- collaborate with others in the course of such analyses and presentations

The programmes aim to provide students with the opportunity to engage with the range of expertise and internationally recognized research undertaken in the Dept. of Philosophy. Through these various aims and provisions, the programmes will enrich the lives of students who take them, and will provide society with the resource of graduates who can think and express their thoughts in a clear and logical manner. Graduates equipped with these transferable skills as well as with the knowledge of the subject's contents will be employed in a wide range of occupations.
For Year Abroad programme only
In addition to the aims of the 3-year BA programme, the 4-year programme has aims to:
- To give students the opportunity to live in the society and culture of a foreign country;
- To provide the opportunity to learn a foreign language/improve existing proficiency (where applicable);
- To acquire the ability to study authors of interest in their original language (where applicable);
- To provide the opportunity to experience academic life in general, and philosophy in particular, as it is practised in another country;
- To enhance students' organisation and communication skills;
- To enhance students' employability through proven ability to succeed in a foreign setting;
- To provide an extra opportunity for students to study in more depth topics of particular interest to them.
For Year in Computer Science programme only:

Computer Science is both an academic discipline in its own right and an enabling technology for other disciplines: Arts, Humanities and Social Sciences as well as Science and Engineering. The focus here is firmly on Computer Science as an enabling technology. The programme aims to provide a solid, self-contained and coherent core of computer science suitable for combination with a variety of other academic disciplines. It aims to provide:
- A grounding in the theory underpinning modern developments in computer science;
- An introduction to practical software design and implementation.

aims: The Programme's purpose is to equip learners with the know-how to further their leadership skills & business acumen, to be better prepared in their own career, & a valuable asset to their organisation & industry. The Programme has been designed to support the needs of those working or intending to work in the sport business sector & sport-related industries.

The Programme aims are to allow learners to achieve more themselves & from others by developing principles & models for leadership; develop skills, knowledge & business expertise to achieve their own goals, those of others, or of a wider organisation or business; develop more effective operational systems & structures to support sustained performance; & develop approaches & methods that better support people, teams & relationships, & culture of the workplace.

The Programme has distinctive features unique to sport & the business of sport i.e., the unique nature of it, of promoting, preparing & improving performance, & the sustainability & vitality of sport as a business sector. Sport & competition illustrate concepts that are applicable in all business, but sport exposes them in unique ways & has distinctive effects on society.

The Programme learning experiences draw from the cohorts? experiences, needs & context. There is prominence upon reflective practice, critical thinking, working collaboratively across multi & interdisciplinary teams, & moving beyond the academic knowledge to apply the technical skill into practical organisational & business effectiveness. Problem-solving is emphasised throughout, drawing from real-world case studies, short-term placement opportunities (1-4 weeks), consultancy challenges & expert-masterclasses. This allows rich perspective & authenticity, offering significant value to the learner, their practice, & to their organisation
Skills & Experiences essential for business, management & leadership, include:
?Technical Skills: master subject-specific knowledge across the business of sport.
?Project Management: design, implement, & evaluate initiatives with different business stakeholders, both public & professional.
?Research & Analysis Skills: conduct rigorous scientific research, data collection, analysis, & interpretation.
?Communication: engage stakeholders, professionals & lay groups, listening effectively & conveying complex information clearly, appropriately & persuasively.
?Critical Thinking & Problem-Solving: address complex business & organisational scenarios, making informed judgements.
?Collaboration & Teamwork: work effectively as a team, co-ordinating interdisciplinary skills to solve business challenges.
?Leadership: support & develop others, mentoring & assessing; work strategically & with integrity.

Enhanced prospects for graduate employment by gaining an MSc from a world-leading school in sport, together with input from a triple crown business school. Preparation for roles within the sports management sector, such as:
?Service Delivery: manage & lead the provision of services related to the sport.
?Industry: within private business to develop commercial impact.
?Non-profit Sectors & Governmental: within sport-related organisations championing advocacy, policymaking, & using the power of sport to improve societal outcomes.
?Events & Facilities: event management & promotion; venues & facilities.
?Player-agent, Sponsorship, & Procurement: develop the commercial aspects of sport, brand management & marketing.
?Sport Administration: roles in regional, national & international sporting organisations, developing strategy operations in sport.
?Research Scientist: conduct research in academic or industry settings, contribute to the advancement of knowledge in business, management, & leadership.
?PhD Programmes: pursue further academic research & specialisation through doctoral studies in business, leadership, management.

data.shortTitle: MSc Dev Sci & Neurodivers FT
aims: The aim of the programme is to provide Master's level teaching and research supervision in Psychology. The programme is directed at students with an undergraduate degree in psychology, who wish to extend their understanding of developmental science and neurodiversity.
A core component of the course involves research labs where students get hands-on, face-to-face contact with research activity.
Students will be able to choose from a range of master level core modules that specialise in developmental science and neurodiversity.

Although students will experience formal learning in large and small groups, much of the course is focused on informal learning by experiencing research in psychology first hand. Students will have opportunities to get to know the more advanced members of lab teams and participate directly in on-going research activity.

Students will improve their ability to use computers for research activity, review the literature, critical reading skills, and written and oral presentations. They will have an opportunity to gain specialist training in computer programming, data science methods and data analysis (e.g. structural equation modelling)
The aims of the programme are:
? To equip students with statistical knowledge and tools used in psychology in general and developmental science in particular.
? To provide opportunities for in depth study of optional specialised topics which are at the cutting edge of research: e.g. neurodiversity, quantitative research methods for studying development
? To foster a sense of excitement in neurodiversity as an approach to understanding diversity in psychological functions and development.
? To provide master level training in research methods leading to competence in research design, data collection, analysis, statistics, interpretation and reporting,
? To develop students? awareness to the open science framework and its implication in day to day research.
? To enable students to conduct an independent research project under the supervision of academic staff.
? To teach students how to communicate research in various formats (e.g. conference poster, writing manuscript for peer review journal, oral presentation).

outcome: 1. 3. Demonstrate knowledge and understanding for research on development and change across the full human lifespan. (Applicable to the following qualifications: PGCert; PGDip; MSc Developmental Science and Neurodiversity )
4. Scientific principles and methodologies for a broad range of research. (Applicable to the following qualifications: PGCert; PGDip; MSc Developmental Science and Neurodiversity )

aims: Understanding climate and environmental change, how we address its causes, how we live with and respond to its impacts, and how we find sustainable solutions to our use of Earth's resources and impacts of planetary systems, is one of the most pressing issues facing humanity. This one-year programme aims to introduce environmentally motivated students studying in a range of disciplines to the core concepts of environmental change and sustainability, from the perspective of planetary processes and environments impacts, and in terms of developing sustainable solutions to present-day challenges. In an increasingly globalised world, it is of paramount importance that we are able to develop sustainable and interdisciplinary approaches across management of energy, natural resources, food security, biodiversity, ecology, and natural hazards.

Tackling themes across environmental sustainability requires a broad and interdisciplinary approach, and a working knowledge of Earth and Environmental processes and the intersection of human pressures on ecological systems. This one year of study meets this need by providing students with a broad foundation in Earth and Environmental Science and Biosciences, giving the student a working introduction to sustainability challenges alongside a range of transferable cross-disciplinary skills that will support students? skills and careers irrespective of discipline.  The constituent modules introduce the necessary understanding and skills to address the challenges posed by global environmental change and aim to take an interdisciplinary and practical approach.

Graduates who have added this additional year to their existing programme will enter their final year with a different perspective on their core studies and will be equipped for a wider range of graduate employment.

aims: The MA in Digital Media and Creative Industries is a cutting-edge, applied- and engaged-programme, shaped around concepts of engagement, diversity, creativity and sustainability, and designed to equip students with the skills and knowledge needed to thrive in the rapidly evolving landscape of digital media and creative sectors.

This innovative, industry-shaped programme draws on research and practice-led expertise in film and media production design, arts and cultural policy, and the legal, administrative and management dimensions of the creative industries. It blends theoretical and academic study with the realities of contemporary creative and cultural production to provide graduates with a firm grounding in all aspects of working in the sector, drawing on the School's substantial connections with creative and cultural partners in the region.

Through industry-led sessions, delivered by partners in the region, the programme will offer significant networking opportunities for students, ensure that students are connected to the latest ideas in a fast-paced sector with industry links providing the opportunity of working in collaboration with external stakeholders in the research component of their degree.
The programme will cover a range of topics related to Digital Media and Creative Industries, such as:
Core Digital Media Foundations:  the core concepts and theories underpinning digital media and how technology is transforming the creative industries.
Legal and Legislative approaches to the Creative and Cultural Sector: contemporary legal issues in the industry, such as copyright, digital rights and conservation law.
Digital Content Creation: Learn hands-on skills in digital content creation, including video production, graphic design, and interactive media development.
Media Entrepreneurship: Explore the business side of the creative industries, from entrepreneurship and startups to intellectual property and digital marketing.
Emerging Technologies: Stay ahead of the curve by studying emerging technologies such as virtual reality, augmented reality, and artificial intelligence, and their impact on digital media.
Industry Immersion: Engage in real-world projects and internships with leading media and creative companies, gaining practical experience and building a professional network.

Graduates of this program will possess a diverse set of transferable and industry specific skills, including digital content creation, project management, data analytics, and critical thinking. They will be adept at navigating the digital landscape and will be well-prepared to adapt to new technologies and trends. This skillset and knowledge will leave them well-positioned for careers in the cultural and creative industries, including:
Digital marketing and advertising
Media production and broadcasting
Content strategy and management
Startups and entrepreneurship in the creative industries
Further academic research or Ph.D. studies in related fields

aims: The programme is designed for health care professionals (and others who have the relevant knowledge base / experience) who intend to follow a career path in which clinical / health research plays a major part. For the majority of those taking the programme the MRes will be a preparatory step towards doctoral studies.

The programme aims to provide students with an opportunity to develop and demonstrate research skills appropriate to clinical and related health environments. The core taught component of the programme is designed to provide students with generic research knowledge and skills: a knowledge base / skill set that can be broadened out through access to a range of optional M Level modules in research or in topics relevant to the field of research of the individual student.

The research component provides students with a supervised opportunity to apply and continue to develop the knowledge and skills they have gained from the taught component through a major research project.

The MRes Clinical Research is currently only available as an exit qualification for doctors admitted to the Academic Clinical Fellows (ACF) framework. Whilst this would continue to be a route of entry, this submission proposes that the renamed degree MRes Clinical / Health Research should also be available as a stand alone programme admitting doctors from outside the ACF and other health professionals.

The programme aims to provide a flexible educational framework from which students with varying experience and varying learning needs can draw the training they require to support them in their development as researchers / academics and prepare them to undertake a PhD.

aims: The MRes in Biomedical Sciences programme is aimed at life science students who wish to develop research careers in a range of biomedical disciplines. The programme will provide the student with an in-depth knowledge of the field that they have chosen as their discipline area and allow them to gain practical experience working as part of leading research groups within the participating departments in the College of Medicine and Heath. The programme comprises a 60 credit taught element consisting of a 40 credit subject specialist module (determined by the research theme the student selects) and a core Research Skills module taken by all students.  The themes are Cardiovascular Sciences, Inflammation and Aging, Neurogenetics, Immunology and Neuropharmacology.  It is anticipated that over time additional themes will be incorporated into this programme and the clear framework will make this more achievable for new themes.

In the discipline specific module, students will be exposed to research-led teaching by academics in the area - they will be given a fundamental grounding in the subject area as well as learning about the cutting-edge research being undertaken by the academics within that theme.  The core research skills module will give the student a range of essential skills which will underpin their research project, including experimental design, data interpretation and presentation, critical analysis of the literature, statistics, bioinformatics and the introduction to a variety of fundamental techniques. After completing the taught components, students will start their 120 credit research project hosted by a research group aligned to their theme of choice.  Students will be embedded in their research groups for 9 months and this element of the programme is part of the post-graduate research degree pathway.  The culmination of the project will the preparation of thesis that will be examined by experts in their field.  Students will have opportunities to attend conferences to present their work and it is anticipated that their work will contribute to scientific outputs by their host laboratories.   It is expected that this programme will be highly attractive and relevant to students who wish to further their postgraduate studies at PhD level but also to students wishing to pursue alternative scientific career pathways. Thus, the programme will provide students with a strong grounding subject discipline and allow them to become stronger candidates for PhD programmes and other research positions.

data.school: School of Geog Earth & Env Sci
aims: The core aim of this programme is to train the next generation of urban planners who will need to adopt a multi- and inter-disciplinary approach in order to address contemporary challenges and solve associated problems faced by urban regions. Drawing upon GEES? world leading expertise in Planning, Environmental Science, Public Health and Critical Urban Studies, the programme will provide the necessary understanding, skills and knowledge that planners in government, private enterprises, NGOs and communities will need to provide innovative solutions to complex issues that impact upon a diverse range of stakeholders.
Key areas of understanding and skills that students will develop during the programme include:
? Challenges urban areas face in the delivery of sustainable, inclusive and healthy places and what measures can be put in place to mitigate these
? Opportunities and threats posed to urban areas by globalising trends, new technologies and the rapid rate of societal change

? Impact of urban growth on the natural environment such as atmospheric pollution, water quality plastic pollution etc., and the various approaches that are under development to mitigate related pressures. Within this area as well an understanding of the approaches that urban areas are taking to ensure post-carbon futures
? Changing living patterns in urban areas, the role and nature of migration, social polarisation, social disadvantage and spatial fragmentation, and how the needs of diverse communities can be met

These themes will be pursued across all modules and together will provide a holistic approach to the challenge of contemporary urban planning. To enable this, a wide-range of teaching approaches will be utilised such as lectures, seminars, practitioner talks, site visits, field work and studio work - an emphasis will be placed on teaching that engages with the `real world? as much as possible, utilising Dubai as an urban laboratory. Reflecting this, assessments will be authentic and involve living case studies ? this will enhance not only understanding and skills but also employability.

Planning as a career is developing beyond its traditional employment pathways in view of the increasing importance of the sustainability agenda and the impacts of urban expansion on the environment and society more broadly. The programme will therefore enable the effective development a new generation of planners who will be able to provide a more holistic, sustainability-focussed, approach to urban development and the mitigation of existing environmental and societal issues. To enable this, all of the modules will take an interdisciplinary approach to the subject matter ensuring that graduates will be able to articulate the science behind critical urban issues, such as atmospheric pollution, and be confident in providing solutions. Therefore, graduates or the programme will be highly sought after not just in traditional planning spheres, such as planning consultancies and government agencies, but also in NGOs, international organisations (e.g. World Bank/UN), and in the emerging sustainability sectors within large corporate organisations.

data.longTitle: Drama and Creative Writing with Year Abroad
aims: BA Drama and Creative Writing is characterised by a wide study, which is methodologically- and theoretically- informed, of Creative Writing, ranging across genres, modes and media, combined with the theoretical and practical exploration of a wide range of theatrical and performance styles, from British playwrights and actor training to immersive practices and directing.

Students will develop a deep and rich understanding of the generative, compositional and self-reflective processes involved in creative work in both disciplines, learning practical, technical and industry-specific skills en route. Students will also engage critically with the history and thematic dimensions of both disciplines, encountering a wide range of approaches to Drama and Creative Writing in different historical periods. In the third year, students will have the opportunity to take the Professional Skills Module, to undertake a placement or progress their own entrepreneurial project.
The programme aims to produce individuals who possess a broad range of knowledge and understanding of Drama and Creative Writing. It will give students the opportunity to:
Develop analytical and practical skills derived from close reading of a wide range of texts and critical studies.
Gain skills in writing, reasoning, presentation, performance and independent research.
Work creatively through writing and performance practices to explore a diversity of ways of engaging different audiences .
Understand the creative and political potential of writing and performance as cultural and social practices .
.Understand the histories, cultures and practices of writing and performance, informed by key theoretical approaches.
Develop self-reflective practices in writing and performance, taking account of artistic processes and discoveries
Develop interpersonal and communication skills, with particular strengths in collaboration and teamwork
Gain an understanding of how to narrate these skills to future employers.

The wide range of reasoning, research, independent learning, communication and creative skills acquired from this programme equips graduates to pursue further study or employment in Drama and Creative Writing related disciplines, and is readily transferable to a variety of commercial, cultural and professional careers, including the creative arts, publishing, film or media sectors.
For semester/year abroad programmes only:

Study abroad will provide students with the opportunity to immerse themselves in the society and culture of a foreign country while gaining experience of a different academic environment and way of teaching. Study abroad also provides an opportunity for students to improve their existing language proficiency (where applicable) as well as enhancing their organisation and communication skills and their employability through a proven ability to succeed in an unfamiliar setting.
For Year in Civic Leadership only:

The Year in Civic Leadership allows students to put into practice the theoretical knowledge and skills developed during their academic studies, and to critically reflect on this activity, by devising a civic engagement project in collaboration with local community actors. The modules deepen student's appreciation of civic engagement, encouraging them to think about how they can enrich the communities they live and work in.

aims: To enable students to achieve the appropriate level of the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (specified by language under Learning Outcomes) through the systematic integration of language and content teaching.
To enable students to explain and assess critically the multi-disciplinary features and significance of the culture, history and society of their chosen language communities.

To enable students to be digitally literate. Students will be able to use appropriate, up-to-date technology in the effective learning of languages and to understand works of culture (understood in the broadest sense, to include history, society, politics, and other material covered in modules aligned with the Birmingham Languages Graduate).
To enable students to handle and analyse material relating to research projects based in the Department of Modern Languages.
*To enable students to engage with appropriately adapted questions derived from research projects based in the Department of Modern Languages.
To enable students to become effective independent learners, with regular opportunities to develop skills in research, academic writing, and reflective learning.

To enable students to be competitively employable through the acquisition of direct and transferable skills as well as through: 1) appropriate integration of Modern Languages careers topics within core modules; 2) optional placement opportunities relating to Modern Languages (credit-bearing and non-credit-bearing); 3) non-credit bearing Modern Languages careers events.
*To enable students to give a persuasive account of their degree and of why they have assembled their degree in a particular way.

To provide students with language and language-related transferable skills useful in a range of contexts, both educational and professional; and to respond to national and international needs for advanced strategic competence in a variety of world languages.
To enable students to acquire first-hand experience of living and studying and/ or working abroad.

To enable students to develop a wide range of transferable skills, including the assimilation, analysis, organisation and synthesis of information and its effective communication in speech and writing, through the study of complex material, which can be applied in a variety of educational and professional contexts, thereby meeting a national and international need for competence in modern foreign languages.
Students  can study:

one language to 120 credits (Advanced French, Advanced German, Advanced Italian, Advanced Spanish only) to include departmental optional modules; two languages or one language plus Translation Studies (some languages only allow 40 credits per year, others permit up to 80 credits); three languages or two languages plus Translation Studies
A compulsory period of residence abroad.

Exemption from the year abroad: In exceptional circumstances, students may be granted an exemption from the compulsory year abroad. Where students taking three languages are exempted from the Year Abroad, the normal expectation would be that the student would only continue with two languages into final year.
Students studying English as a Modern Foreign Language can study:
three languages equally weighted (40/40/40);
two languages equally weighted (60/60);
two languages with one weighted more heavily than the other (80/40).
English can only be combined with Beginners or Advanced French, Beginners or Advanced German, Beginners or Advanced Spanish or Beginners Chinese.
The following languages cannot be taken together for timetabling reasons:
Pillar 1: English as a Modern Foreign Language (EMFL), Italian, Japanese and Russian
Pillar 2: Chinese Mandarin, German and Portuguese
Pillar 4: French and Catalan Minor
Translation Studies with Advanced Russian as your only Advanced language. Languages in the same pillar cannot be taken together.

aims: The outline aims of the programme are:

To provide advanced engineering skills and knowledge in the broad area of mechanical engineering for a research or development career in the field of mechanical engineering, either in industry or academia.

To provide the opportunity to carry out projects in a range of mechanical engineering subject areas, and thereby to acquire the generic research skills necessary to engage in future research or study.

To provide the student with knowledge of recent advances and methods in core mechanical engineering subjects including Advanced Mechanics and Thermal Systems, Advanced Fuel and Powertrain Systems, Advanced Manufacturing, Research and Application of Machining Processes, Industrial Automation and Robotics, Bio-Medical and Micro Engineering, Advanced Vehicle Engineering, and Intelligent Automation.
To provide the student with the experimental and analytical skills to design and evaluate advanced mechanical engineering systems relevant to industry and research.

To educate students to MSc level, accredited as meeting the academic requirement for Further Learning for registration as a Chartered Engineer (CEng); as detailed in the Accreditation of Higher Education Programmes (Fourth edition) (AHEP4).

outcome: The advanced level scientific theories of mechanical and related engineering disciplines including Advanced Mechanics and Thermal Systems, Advanced Fuel and Powertrain Systems, Advanced Manufacturing, Research and Application of Machining Processes, Industrial Automation and Robotics, Bio-Medical and Micro Engineering, Advanced Vehicle Engineering, and Intelligent Automation and other related areas
Mechanical systems and components through the use of analytical methods and modelling techniques at advanced level

mathematical and computer models relevant to the mechanical and related engineering disciplines, and an appreciation of their limitations
current practice in mechanical and related engineering and its limitations and some appreciation of likely new developments;
a wide and extensive range of engineering materials and components

aims: BA Drama and English Literature is a Single Honours Programme, including study in ancilliary disciplines. It is characterised by a wide study, methodologically and theoretically informed, of the range of literature in the English language from the medieval period to the present, and by the theoretical and practical exploration of a wide range of theatrical and performance styles, from the Renaissance stage to the present. It aims to produce individuals who possess a broad range of knowledge and understanding of English literature and performance; critical skills in the close reading and analysis of texts both literary and non-literary; analytical and practical skills derived from the close analysis of dramatic and performance texts and contexts; organisational and presentational skills, including those derived from work on the production and organisational aspects of theatre and performance; and a developed competence in interpersonal and communicative skills, with particular strengths in collaborative work. The wide range of reasoning, research, independent learning, communication and organisational skills acquired from this programme equips graduates to pursue further study or employment in English, Drama and related disciplines, and is readily transferable to a variety of commercial, cultural and professional careers.

aims: The MSc programme in Railway Systems Engineering has been designed to satisfy the following aims: Create a supportive environment where academics and leading practitioners in the railway industry support postgraduate students in acquiring the domain skills and know-how necessary to implement successful railway systems in existing and new contexts; Develop in students a broad understanding of the characteristics of the most significant railway engineering and operational subsystems, ranging from strategic management of technology and ergonomics to detailed technical aspects, such as traction drives and electro-magnetic compatibility;? Provide postgraduate students with the tools to optimise the interaction of components and subsystems; Provide postgraduate students with the approaches and tools necessary to undertake and manage complex systems engineering and integration tasks within the constraints of demanding railway environments; Develop in postgraduate students a range of both generic and subject-specific skills appropriate for employment in most areas of railway engineering and railway project management; Allow postgraduate students to develop their skills in the areas of effective communication and team-working and in the management for individual and group projects; Develop in postgraduate students an independence of thought, intellectual curiosity and a critical approach to evidence, theories and concepts; Encourage the development of an ethical and socially responsible approach to working with stakeholders, both within and outside the railway industry; Encourage postgraduate students to embrace a commitment to life-long learning and self development; Provide teaching that is informed and invigorated by the research and scholarship of the programme staff and that strives to make best use of student-centred and practice-based learning; Create learning situations that allow postgraduates to share experiences and to learn from each other; Assess postgraduate students in a balanced manner across a range of skills, domains of know-how and understanding while identifying and supporting academic excellence; Ensure that part-time students can apply their new skills immediately in their work and that full-time students are ready for their first industry assignments; Enable successful postgraduate students to realise their full potential through gaining a higher degree.

aims: Year in International Business (Dubai)

This BSc Year in International Business (Dubai) programme offers students studying on programmes across the University of Birmingham the opportunity to study for a year at the University of Birmingham Dubai campus and gain a sound understanding of international business management.

Through study on this programme students will gain an understanding of Business Management within a regional and international context as a broad discipline and develop an appreciation of research relevant to that discipline.  Students on this programme will gain intellectual grounding, core knowledge and understanding of international business and it also offers students the opportunity to develop their intellectual skills, analytical skills, problem-solving skills and communication skills which are crucial within the world of business.  Transferable skills are key to this programme where students through formative and summative assessment will develop their communication and team working skills whilst also being provided with a breadth of knowledge of business management.  The underlying philosophy of the programme is that students can study a mix of core 1st year international business management modules, with one module focusing on responsible business, reflecting the School's mission; and choose 3 option modules.  As this programme is unique to the Dubai campus students will be offered the opportunity to study a 10 credit optional module Arabic Language (1).
The skills that students will develop and the experiences they will have are highlighted as follows:
? Apply critical thinking and analytical skills - notably, the ability to filter and assess complex arguments.
? Develop a sensitivity to different international and cultural perspectives within business.
? Critically self-reflect and develop employability and transferable skills.
? Develop communication skills both written and verbal.
Delivery of all modules on this programme will be through a mix of lectures, seminars, class discussions, readings, case studies, media, invited guest speakers and online webinars.

Assessment of the programme will be through formative and summative assessment and will include a mix of assessment methods across the modules, including: formal exams, essays, group work and oral presentations.

On completion of this one year programme students will be equipped with the knowledge and skills that can be utilised when they return to their degree programme, and also after graduation where they may wish to seek employment or further study in the discipline of international business.
Sport, Exercise and Health Sciences
BSc/MSci Sport Exercise and Health Sciences aims to develop and apply knowledge in the sciences of sport, exercise, health and rehabilitation. It embraces our three key research themes:
1. Sport Performance, Policy and Education
2. Exercise, Medicine and Health
3. Human Movement and Rehabilitation
Our interdisciplinary programme aims to explore questions of sport and performance and the role of exercise in promoting and maintaining health throughout the lifespan.

Modules across the school provide the opportunity to study in many areas from both scientific and applied perspectives. Topics included are physiology, biochemistry, psychology and motor control, with the option to take modules in complementary topics such as physical education, coaching, and sociology. More multidisciplinary and interdisciplinary modules are included at year 3 and year 4.

aims: The MA in Cities, Sustainability, and Wellbeing is a taught Master's degree providing specialist research skills and expertise in advanced topics in Human Geography. The programme provides a set of transferable skills that will equip graduates for the employment market and that also provides an ideal foundation for further academic research, including a route for those undertaking a PhD in Human Geography.

The programme draws on specialist Human Geography expertise in GEES, to provide conceptual and methodological research training that is integrated with a distinctive component of empirical research practice, from a variety of contextual and research-intensive teaching and learning.
The aims of the programme are:

To develop an advanced and analytical understanding of recent and contemporary Human Geography conceptual debates, drawing on a suite of geographical ideas and approaches in the global areas of urban spaces, wellbeing and sustainability

To evaluate and apply research methodologies and techniques that are responsible, ethical, and relevant to geographical research, and to design and execute projects in the areas of urban spaces, wellbeing and sustainability

To be able to communicate specialist policy- and industry-relevant ideas and research evidence around global challenges, in a variety of styles and formats and to a suite of academic and non-academic audiences.

The programme content spans a number of urban, wellbeing and sustainability challenges at a variety of scales across the Global North and Global South, including: environmental change, urban sustainability, migration, armed conflict, and security and counterterrorism.

Graduates of the MA in Cities, Sustainability, and Wellbeing will acquire discipline-specific skills that will enable them to progress further into a range of academic and non-academic career pathways. These include, among others, careers in sectors shaping policy, governance, and socioeconomic growth.

aims: The first two years of the course builds a detailed understanding of how the human body functions and what can go wrong in disease. The content extends from the single cell to the whole body. The students begin to learn about major pathologies such as cancer, cardiovascular disease, neurodegenerative disease, arthritis and diabetes, and the genetic basis of inherited disorders.?

All students take a common set of key subjects which will provide them with the core knowledge to understand the importance of each of the major disciplines of medical science. This forms a strong foundation for their final year. In addition, throughout the course students develop core research skills, such as key technical skills, problem solving ability, data analysis and interpretations, helping them develop an understanding of the key ethical and social issues surrounding medical science.

In the second year there will be an opportunity to specialise in a scientific area of their choice, linked to the College major research themes. This student selected component will allow an in-depth exploration of the area under the guidance of one of our subject experts. The themes will include cancer, neuroscience, infection and immunity, pharmacology and cardiovascular science. This will provide a platform for further specialisation in the third year.

At the end of the second year there is the possibility of taking a year out to gain work experience, by securing a placement in, for example, the pharmaceutical industry. Students may also opt to undertake a summer research project within the College.

During the first term of their final year, students specialise by selecting one taught option from over 20 specialist modules in a wide range of subject areas, including different aspects of neuroscience, cancer, virology, cardiovascular science, pharmacology, endocrinology, stem cell biology, ageing and immunology. Students learn about the latest findings and are exposed to advanced research techniques, guided by internationally recognised experts in these fields. Students undertake a compulsory module in Experimental Data Interpretation to consolidate research skills and to enhance statistical testing and implementation on large research data sets.

These taught options lead on to a substantial research project in the spring term, which in the majority of cases is laboratory based specifically within one of our leading research active laboratories. Students work independently, under supervision, for ten weeks full-time on an original piece of research, acquiring and analysing their own data. The project develops and enhances not just their practical and analytical abilities, but also a range of other skills that will be a key to success in whatever career path they choose. Students undertake a final compulsory module; Global Challenge which enhances students team communication and allows an innovative and creative approach to problem solving within the Biomedical field.

aims: The BA Ancient and Medieval History offers students a unique opportunity to acquire an understanding of historical events and processes via a specific study of the ancient and medieval histories of Europe, , and of the wider world. In so doing, the programme develops a range of analytical and organisational skills, independent and critical thinking, and the ability to synthesise and communication information and ideas. These attributes will be developed through three interlocked strands of the curriculum:
The programme aims to::
facilitate intellectual development by encouraging independence and critical thinking;
provide a foundation for research into and further study of the past;

develop an innovative range of subject specific and transferable skills in research, analysis and presentation through the study and understanding of ancient and medieval history in the context of cognate disciplines;
instil sensitivity to the range of cultural similarities and differences that is of particular importance and value in ancient, medieval and modern multicultural societies;
provide the opportunity to study relevant ancient languages;
provide the broadest possible platform of transferable skills for both further study and intellectual training outside the academy.

The programme also attunes students to contemporary challenges within and beyond the discipline - globalisation; sustainability; inequalities ? to the importance of thinking critically about heritage, conservation, and the place of the past in public life. As such diversity is the heart of the curriculum. The programme recovers and reintegrates the voices of those previously marginalised by virtue of race, gender, sexuality, (dis)ability, or excluded by virtue of dominant narratives of the past; it  enables and encourages students to explore the histories and cultures of different peoples, societies, and cultures from around the world.

The programme facilitates the development of a wide and diverse range of transferable skills - in research, in analysis, in evaluation and synthesis, in organisation, and in communication ? and thus prepares students both for further study and for a wide range of careers within and beyond the academy. These may include teaching (from primary to higher education), museums and galleries, heritage management, tourism, creative economy, and government work.
For year abroad only:

Study abroad will provide students with the opportunity to immerse themselves in the society and culture of a foreign country while gaining experience of a different academic environment and way of teaching. aims: The MSc in Urban Analytics for Planners is designed to equip students with advanced skills in data analysis and modelling, with a specific focus on their application to urban planning and transport systems. This programme emphasises the integration of quantitative methods with urban theory and practice, preparing students to address the complex challenges that cities face in an increasingly data-driven world. At the core of the programme is a focus on using data analytics to inform smart urban planning decisions that enhance sustainability, mobility, and the overall quality of urban life.

Students will develop a comprehensive understanding of the role of data in shaping urban environments, from the collection and analysis of large datasets to the application of spatial models and visualization techniques. This programme will attract individuals from diverse backgrounds, including planners, engineers, and data scientists, who are eager to leverage their technical expertise to address pressing urban issues. Through a combination of theoretical study and practical application, students will be prepared to lead in the development of data-driven solutions for cities, ensuring that their designs are not only functional but also sustainable and resilient.

Throughout the programme, students will first build a solid foundation in urban planning before progressing to specialised tools and practical skills in urban analytics. In the second semester, students will collaborate with peers from related disciplines in an integrated Urban Lab, working on real-world urban projects. This hands-on experience, supervised by industry professionals, will equip students with the practical skills and professional insight necessary to excel in the growing field of urban analytics.

Graduates of the MSc Data Analytics for Urban Planners programme will be uniquely positioned for careers at the intersection of data science, transport planning, and urban planning and development. As cities increasingly rely on data-driven solutions to address mobility, sustainability, and growth challenges, graduates will be highly sought after for roles in government agencies, consultancy firms, urban analytics companies, and transport planning organisations. Their ability to apply advanced data analytics to complex urban systems will make them key contributors to the future of urban planning and design. To achieve this, all modules will take an interdisciplinary approach, ensuring that graduates can articulate the science behind critical urban issues, and confidently offer solutions. As a result, graduates of this programme will be highly sought after, not only in traditional planning roles within consultancies and government agencies but also in NGOs, international organizations (e.g., World Bank, UN), and emerging sustainability sectors within large corporations.

aims: The BSc is accredited by the Royal Society of Chemistry for partially satisfying the academic requirements for the award of CChem.

The Programme develops chemical, intellectual and transferable skills, preparing students for employment in chemical and related fields.  The educational aims of the programme are informed by the Chemistry benchmarking statements and the accreditation criteria of the Royal Society of Chemistry.
In more detail, the programme aims to:

Provide a broad and balanced knowledge base in the field of chemistry, to additionally provide a grounding in related disciplines studied (e.g. optional material), and to develop wider transferable and transformation skills;
Provide a rational, structured and coherent programme of study that is relevant to the needs of employers;
Facilitate the professional development of the student and provide training in appropriate skills;
Develop a logical and enquiring attitude, with appropriate critical analysis and scientific discipline to encourage lifelong learning;
Provide experience of originality in the application of knowledge and an understanding of how research techniques are used to create and interpret knowledge in Chemistry;
Develop an enthusiasm for Chemistry, and expose students to the frontiers of the discipline;
Generate in students an appreciation of the importance of the application of chemistry in industrial, economic, environmental and social contexts;
Provide academic research experience through completion of a research project, and provide experience of research in an industrial context through completion of an industrial project.

outcome: Structure, Reactivity and Bonding, Determination of Structure, Analytical Chemistry
Chemistry of the Elements, s-, p-, and d- block elements, Transition Metal Chemistry, Solid-State Chemistry, Organometallic Chemistry, Homogeneous Catalysis, f- block elements.

Synthesis and Mechanism in Organic Chemistry, Determination of Structure using NMR, Physical Organic Chemistry, Reactive Intermediates, Conformational Analysis and Alicyclic Chemistry, FMO Methods and Stereoelectronic effects, Medicinally Active Compounds, Synthetic Strategy and Planning, Functional Group Transformations.

Thermodynamics, Kinetics, Quantum Mechanics and Intramolecular Forces, Properties of Solutions, Electrolyte Solutions and Electrochemistry, Optical Spectroscopy, Electronic Terms and States, Electronic Spectroscopy and Level Populations, Surface Science and Heterogeneous Catalysis, Photochemistry and Kinetics, Properties of Solids and their Surfaces.
Advanced Techniques, Research Methodology, and Research Project.
learning: "The acquisition of knowledge is achieved mainly through lectures, laboratory classes (which supplement and complement the core chemistry material) and directed student-centred learning.
Student-centred learning is employed where there is appropriate source material, and will vary during the levels of the programme.
Support of lecture-based learning is provided by workshops and tutorials, and through set work (e.g. problem sheets, worksheets etc). "
assessment: "Assessment methods as specified in each module guide.
All learning outcomes in a module are assessed, and the mode of assessment specified for each outcome.

In general, each module is assessed by a combination of continuous assessment during the year (e.g. workshop and/or laboratory based assessment) and written unseen examinations, normally at the end of each level.

In Year 3 (the placement year) the Industrial Research Project is assessed on a pass/fail basis only, based on a combination of: regular up-date reports from the Industrial Supervisor; an oral presentation; and a final report (6,000 - 8,000 words)
In Year 4, projects are assessed by dissertation, oral presentation and oral examination. "

outcome: Integrate theoretical concepts and practice;

data.progTitle: MA History (Global History) Part-time.
data.shortTitle: MA History (Global History) PT
aims: 1. This Taught MA in History enables graduate students to develop expertise in a variety of subjects in which the Department of History has significant strengths.(which at present include Medieval Studies; Early Modern History; Global History; US History; Contemporary History; Public History; and Modern British Studies).

2. The programme aims to enable students to acquire a systematic understanding of the subjects they study, and a critical awareness of current problems and/or new insights, much of which is at, or informed by, the forefront of the subjects studied.
3. The programme aims to enable students to acquire a comprehensive understanding of techniques applicable to their own research and advanced scholarship.

4. The programme aims to encourage students to demonstrate originality in the application of knowledge, together with a practical understanding of how established techniques of research and enquiry are used to create and interpret knowledge in the discipline.
5. The programme aims to enable students to acquire a conceptual understanding that allows them to evaluate critically current research and advanced scholarship in the discipline.

6. The programme aims to enable students to develop their skills in research and writing through preparing assessed work and a substantial dissertation written under the supervision of a specialist in the subject.

7. The programme aims to enable students to gain a mixture of generic and discipline-specific skills, providing a solid base both for academic research into History or an allied discipline at doctoral level, and also for the development of a successful professional career, including (but not limited to) fields adjacent to the historical discipline, such as public history and heritage.

8. The programme aims to enable students to specialise in a particular historical pathway, should they wish to, including studying taught modules and writing their dissertation on a topic within the pathway area of specialism.
data.benchmark: UG QAA Subject Benchmark Statement for History (2022)

outcome: 1. Significant chronological, regional and/or thematic topics which engage with complex and challenging problems in the historical discipline generally, and especially with respect to one or more of the following areas: Medieval Studies; Early Modern History; Global History; US History; Contemporary History; Public History; and Modern British Studies. (PGCert/PGDip/MA)
2. Key theoretical and methodological issues enabling students to think critically about the study and practice of academic history. (PGCert/PGDip/MA)

3. The skills and expertise necessary for critically analysing and understanding the value and limitations of  wide range of primary sources appropriate to the topic of study, including (but not limited to) printed and manuscript textual evidence, visual sources, material culture, oral history, etc. (PGDip/MA)

4. The skills involved in the process of researching and writing an original research project in history, including appropriate professional standards in communicating and presenting their research orally and in writing. (MA)
learning: 1-4: Lectures, seminars, personal academic tutorials, one-to-one supervision and independent study
assessment: 1-4: A mixture of assessed essays, written examinations, oral presentation (PGDip and MA only), and a dissertation (MA only)

outcome: 1. To carry out practical historical research using information technology and paper-based sources (MA)
2. To analyse and synthesise relevant material from primary and secondary sources (PGCert/PGDip/MA)

3. To produce academic writing to a high standard of scholarship, including writing effectively in the English language and presenting information and ideas in a manner that meets relevant scholarly conventions (PGCert/PGDip/MA)

4. To apply historical and related knowledge systematically to complex problems by constructing arguments, recognising potential alternative conclusions and providing supporting reasons (PGCert/PGDip/MA)
5. To communicate effectively orally, by giving and receiving information and ideas and modifying responses where appropriate  (PGDip/MA)
6. To think critically and creatively about matters covered in the programme, demonstrating a capacity for independent thinking (PGCert/PGDip/MA)
learning: Preparation for taught modules, including lectures, seminars, one-to-one supervisions, and successful completion of written assessments, oral presentation (PGDip and MA only) & dissertation (MA only).
assessment: Formative written assessment and informal feedback on seminar contributions and class discussion.
Summative assessment via written work including assessed essays, written examinations, and oral presentation.
Formative process of dissertation preparation and supervision (PGDip and MA only) and summative preparation and submission of final dissertation (MA only)

data.progTitle: MSc Sustainable Innovation and Entrepreneurship Part-time.
data.shortTitle: MSc Susta Innov & Entre PT Dub
aims: The MSc Sustainable Innovation and Entrepreneurship programme is for you if you wish to make a difference and foster sustainable and innovative business solutions to address the issues and challenges, such as the drive towards net zero, carbon negativity, equality, diversity and inclusion, of the World of tomorrow and their interconnectedness.

This programme aims to help you develop the critical knowledge, skills, and attributes necessary to tackle the complexity of developing sustainable innovations taking into consideration their environmental, social and economic dimensions implications for businesses, organisations and the wider society; and then implement them either by creating your own business or by contributing to innovation within existing organisations in the private, not-for profit or public sectors.

In doing so, you will be taking a critical and practical approach to sustainable innovation and entrepreneurial endeavours and benefit from the strong research environment of the Birmingham Business School, real case studies and engagement with industry partners, as we well as the support of the University of Birmingham Business Incubator. One of the key elements of the programme will be to help you develop your sustainable entrepreneurial project building on your career aspirations. You will also have the opportunity to interact with other students and professionals from a variety of disciplinary approaches and perspectives offering opportunities for collaboration and networking.
This programme will:
Equip you with the knowledge and skills to develop sustainable innovative solutions across a wide range of industries, sectors, and contexts;
Support you in the development of your own sustainable innovation and/or entrepreneurial career and/or project;

Give you the opportunity to network with like-minded individuals from a variety of disciplinary backgrounds and to cultivate a critical, contextual, and transdisciplinary approach to sustainability, innovation, and entrepreneurship;
Give you access to hand-on experience by working on sustainable and responsible business projects and challenges;
Connect you with the University of Birmingham business incubator programme, the UoB Elevate, and the support it can offer.

One of the distinctive features of this programme is the bootcamp at the beginning of the programme. The bootcamp combines a primer course bringing all functions of the firm while focusing on key skills like cross-cultural management, networking, and career planning. This unique week-long bootcamp will set the scene for the modules that will follow while exploring the experiential learning and hands-on education that is characteristic of the programme. This programme will support you to develop a career promoting and implementing sustainable innovations within existing organisations in the private, not-for profit or public sectors.

After completing this programme, you might progress to either be in a position to create your own sustainable business or organisation or to work in other organisation in roles like Climate Change Analyst, Associate Consultant, Business Development Officer, Project Manager just to name a few. These roles could be in the public, private or charity sectors where there is high demand for graduates who can conduct research, analyse information and formulate and execute programmes of activity, or you may become a Start-up Entrepreneur.
data.benchmark: QAA (2015) for Master?s Degrees in Business and Management

outcome: Critically evaluate the definitions, approaches, and values connected with sustainability and responsible management, innovation and entrepreneurship and assess how these are interrelated, how these can translate into specific cultural, social, economical and political contexts and relate this to their own entrepreneurial aspirations.
Synthetise data and information to analyse and operationalise the interconnectedness between sustainability and innovation within and across various organisations.

Apply sustainability tools and frameworks to responsible business practices and different strategic decision-making linked to with business innovation and /or addressing sustainable development and societal challenges.
Critically evaluate, select, and apply theories and business model frameworks relating to entrepreneurship, corporate entrepreneurship, and sustainable entrepreneurship.
Create a sustainable entrepreneurship business plan, or sustainable project for innovation within an existing organisation.
Critically evaluate managerial theory and practice within organisational environments driven by a sustainability and an innovative ethos.
Evaluate the different forms of policy and regulations and their impact on innovation and entrepreneurship.
Assess key operational functions of business and organisations through the prism of sustainability.
Identify and deal with complex problems to address societal challenges linked to combining sustainable and innovative solutions in fast moving and competitive ecosystems.
learning: Lectures, seminars discussions, presentations, case studies and workshops.

aims: Social Policy investigates the actions and inactions of a range of actors and organisations in the pursuit of human wellbeing. It pays particular attention to a range of problems which cause diswelfare and examines the systems and relationships that seek to end suffering and misery. The discipline requires a level of complexity which not only engages with key fields of welfare (poverty, unemployment, health, housing and education) but also the development of new topics and debates in a rapidly changing, global context. Understanding the pursuit of human wellbeing requires an engagement with ideological debates, conceptual differences and conflicting evidence, all of which are involved and drawn upon within the policy process to create the interventions which enhance (or diminish) wellbeing.    The social policy degree at Birmingham enables students to understand the nature of social problems in the UK and beyond. It encourages students to not only develop an understanding of contemporary social issues but investigate potential solutions and how to promote change to tackle social problems.   Social policy is constantly shifting and changing. In recent years there has been a plethora of organisations engaged in the generation of ideas and policies to address social problems. The subject of social policy therefore must rise to the challenge of equipping its students to not only understand but also engage in the process of policy reform and change. Consequently its requires an approach which embeds students in key concepts and topics of social policy alongside the analytical skills necessary for understanding and informing the policy process.   Constant flux in the sector requires that students be equipped with a range of conceptual, methodological and analytical tools suited to both academic study and the wider demands of employment within a range of sectors which interact with the policy process.   Moreover, Social Policy represents a key aspect of the social sciences, to not only understand the world, but to seek to change it. Students must therefore graduate with the capability of understanding and investigating the causes of human misery and the consequences of policies which seek to its remedy. Consequently, social policy studies the way societies determine the various basic human needs of their populations and the arrangements that are made to meet those needs. Such needs include having sufficient to eat, somewhere to live, a sustainable and safe environment, good health and health care, provision for those who cannot live a fully independent life, education and training and the opportunity for individuals to fully participate in their society.    An important aspect of such studies requires students to engage with the wider mixed economy of welfare. To appreciate that the state is not the only actor involved in the provision of welfare services. An appreciation of the role of the state in relation to the market whilst central to the historical development of social policy must now be broadened to consider additional providers, such as the Third Sector. Social Policy at Birmingham seeks to bring this into an appreciation of the subject alongside the key theoretical and conceptual debates which make the routes to human welfare unclear and uncertain.   Engaging students in this subject (and in line with the QAA benchmarks for the subject) the study of social policy at Birmingham develops a particular pathway through its core modules. The ambition is to create critically aware and engaged students pursing the achievement of social justice (in its various definitions) through policy implementation. This requires a gradual development of students by first introducing students to key topics, concepts and problems facing the UK in a contemporary global context.  "

aims: The MSc in Sustainable Urban Planning and Design provides advanced training in urban planning and design, with an emphasis on global practices in sustainable placemaking. At the programme's core is a focus on creating urban places that prioritise people and sustainability. This programme not only covers the foundational principles, theory, and practices of modern urban planning, but also equips students with the critical skills needed for designing urban environments that are sustainable, liveable, diverse, and resilient. Students will gain a deep understanding of the processes, and principles, involved in sustainable urban planning and design, as well as an appreciation for the evolving nature of the field and the ongoing cycles of placemaking. The programme addresses the global relevance of sustainable design as a discipline within urban planning.

The student journey is designed to support the development of core and foundations knowledge and skills initially, followed by the opportunity to developer deeper skills and knowledge is applied learning environment. The programme is designed as an RTPI Accredited Combined Award planning course, and interfaces through the core modules and dissertation with the established MSc Urban and Regional Planning but offers a unique and globally important emphasis upon sustainable placemaking within the LES/GEES PG portfolio. The course embraces inter-disciplinarity, including through module sharing with further GEES PG courses, enabling an aware and shared learning experience. Real-world practice at both local and regional scales is integral to the programme, ensuring that graduates are prepared to deliver sustainable design solutions in urban and regional contexts.

This programme will equip the next generation of urban planners internationally with a deep knowledge of urban issues and a strong commitment to sustainable placemaking. Students, across all modules, will engage with key contemporary global challenges, particularly those related to sustainability, climate change, housing, nature-based solutions, mobilities, energy, environmental impact, and health and well-being.

The programme seeks to attract graduates from cognate disciplines and well as those in relevant industries (planning, architecture, landscape architecture, property etc) seeking to develop new knowledge and skills. Graduates of the MSc Sustainable Urban Planning and Design programme will be equipped to lead in the creation of sustainable, resilient, and nature and people-centred urban environments. With a foundation in both theoretical knowledge and practical design skills, graduates will be prepared for roles in a diversity of established public and private sector careers, including urban planning, urban design, and the development industry. They will be sought after for their ability to develop innovative, sustainable design solutions that address the pressing challenges facing of a continuously urbanising world in a context specific manner.  As a result, graduates of this programme will be highly attractive to employers, not only in traditional planning roles, but also in NGOs, international organisations (e.g., World Bank, UN), and emerging sustainability sectors within large corporations.

aims: The first two years of the course builds a detailed understanding of how the human body functions and what can go wrong in disease. The content extends from the single cell to the whole body. The students begin to learn about major pathologies such as cancer, cardiovascular disease, neurodegenerative disease, arthritis and diabetes, and the genetic basis of inherited disorders.

All students take a common set of key subjects which will provide them with the core knowledge to understand the importance of each of the major disciplines of medical science. This forms a strong foundation for transitioning onto the MSci. Throughout the course students develop core research skills, such as key technical skills, problem solving ability, data analysis and interpretations, helping them develop an understanding of the key ethical and social issues surrounding medical science.In the second year there will be an opportunity to specialise in a scientific area of their choice, linked to the College major research themes. This student selected component will allow an in-depth exploration of the area under the guidance of one of our subject experts. The themes will include cancer, neuroscience, infection and immunity, pharmacology and cardiovascular science. This will provide a platform for further specialisation in the third year. Within this module students can also select a business and enterprise project which develops their entrepreneurial skills and develops their communication skills with external business partners. At the end of the second or third year there is the possibility of taking a year out to gain work experience, by securing a placement in, for example, the pharmaceutical industry. Students may also opt to undertake a summer research project within the College.
Further options at the end of the second or third year are to enrol for the Year in Computer Science or the Year in Civic Leadership.
Year in Computer Science:

Computer Science is now a major factor in many businesses, professions, and academic disciplines, as well as in everyday life. From practical ICT to profound principles of computation, a solid grounding in Computer Science can offer improved career potential. The Year in Computer Science offers students from non-computing disciplines the chance to gain in-depth knowledge of computing and enhance their work-based skills through the study of Computer Science
Year in Civic Leadership:

The Year in Civic Leadership provides a transdisciplinary opportunity to develop a variety of professional skills across civic engagement, entrepreneurship, and leadership through a project-based placement.

The year is comprised of three modules that put into practice theoretical knowledge and skills developed during prior academic studies, provide an opportunity to critically reflect on this activity while co-creating a community project with a non-profit organisation or social enterprise.  The series of modules deepen appreciation of civic engagement, encourage students to think about how they can make change and enrich the communities in which we live. They will be introduced to the principles of civic engagement & leadership and become active citizens as they design a collaborative project to explore different policy contexts of a specific social issue.

The first two years will be delivered at both UoB Campus Edgbaston and UoB Campus Dubai or University. The third and fourth years will be delivered at UoB Edgbaston. Year in Computer Science and Year in Civic Leadership options take place after year two or year three on the Edgbaston campus.

In the third year students specialise by selecting a single taught options from over 10 specialist modules in a wide range of subject areas, including different aspects of neuroscience, cancer, virology, cardiovascular science, pharmacology, endocrinology, stem cell biology, ageing and immunology. Students learn about the latest findings and are exposed to advanced research techniques, guided by internationally recognised experts in these fields. Students then a compulsory module in Experimental Research Interpretation that re-enforces students statistical knowledge to handle the analysis of large data sets. These taught options lead on to a translational research module which is underpinned by understanding the legislative process required when moving treatments from the bench to the bedside. This module has a substantial practical element, requiring students to demonstrate advanced competencies within the laboratory and to demonstrate and acquire their Good clinical laboratory certificate. The final module in year 3 is the Global challenge, allowing team work to develop students creativity and innovative thinking to resolve a biomedical issue using modern technology. In the final year, students choose aptional modules around emerging technologies within the Biomedical field (e.g. omics, bioinformatics).

The final module is the research project in the which in the majority of cases is laboratory based specifically within one of our leading research active laboratories. Students work independently, under supervision, for 15 weeks full-time on an original piece of research, acquiring and analysing their own data. The project develops and enhances not just their practical and analytical abilities, but also a range of other skills that will be a key to success in whatever career path they choose.
