outcome: Engagement with texts, primary and secondary: By the end of L C: the ability to demonstrate confidence in studying and critically analysing whole novels, plays, poems and films of different kinds and lengths; By the end of L I: the ability to read and locate literary texts from different periods and genres; By the end of L H: the ability to synthesise a wide range of primary and secondary reading and the ability to range independently in their reading beyond prescribed texts in order to diversify and contextualise their study evidenced in a piece of independent research.

The capacity for independent thought and judgement, and the ability to handle information and argument in a critical and self-reflective manner. By the end of L C, the ability to discuss the rationale for key differences between university-level literary study and the methods and expectations experienced at earlier stages of education, and to apply critical and theoretical approaches to the reading of texts; By the end of L I, the ability to construct arguments informed by, but not dependent upon, secondary material; By the end of L H, the ability to construct detailed, balanced and substantiated critical arguments, to locate those arguments in their appropriate scholarly fields and to formulate independent research questions.

The ability independently to use libraries, catalogues, bibliographies and other appropriate reference sources; to make appropriate use of the internet, the e-library, the physical library and other appropriate libraries; and to choose and use suitable editions of literary texts, applying a basic understanding of textual transmission, evidenced by the ability to document, cite and present, according to an agreed stylesheet of scholarly written work.

aims: BSc Economics and Political Science is based in the Department of Economics and it is taught jointly with the Department of Political Science and International Studies.

This programme provides students with an understanding of economic concepts, principles and tools, and their application along with the acquisition of specialist knowledge in theory and practice of politics, political science and public policy.

The programme aims to stimulate students intellectually through the study of economics and political science and to lead them to appreciate its application to a range of problems and its relevance in a variety of contexts. Students should receive a firm foundation of knowledge about the workings of economic systems and develop the relevant skills for the constructive use of that knowledge in a range of settings.

The programme provides students with a range of analytical tools that are applicable to the study of Economics and political science, and transferable to other areas, including analytical and quantitative skills and an ability to develop simplifying frameworks for studying the real world. On graduating, students will be well prepared to work in a range of graduate careers, for example in banking, finance or general management careers, or to progress to Masters-level study.

aims: The aim of the programme is to provide Master's level teaching and research supervision in Psychology. The programme is directed at students with an undergraduate degree in psychology, who wish to extend their understanding of developmental science and neurodiversity.
A core component of the course involves research labs where students get hands-on, face-to-face contact with research activity.
Students will be able to choose from a range of master level core modules that specialise in developmental science and neurodiversity.

Although students will experience formal learning in large and small groups, much of the course is focused on informal learning by experiencing research in psychology first hand. Students will have opportunities to get to know the more advanced members of lab teams and participate directly in on-going research activity.

Students will improve their ability to use computers for research activity, review the literature, critical reading skills, and written and oral presentations. They will have an opportunity to gain specialist training in computer programming, data science methods and data analysis (e.g. structural equation modelling)
The aims of the programme are:
? To equip students with statistical knowledge and tools used in psychology in general and developmental science in particular.
? To provide opportunities for in depth study of optional specialised topics which are at the cutting edge of research: e.g. neurodiversity, quantitative research methods for studying development
? To foster a sense of excitement in neurodiversity as an approach to understanding diversity in psychological functions and development.
? To provide master level training in research methods leading to competence in research design, data collection, analysis, statistics, interpretation and reporting,
? To develop students? awareness to the open science framework and its implication in day to day research.
? To enable students to conduct an independent research project under the supervision of academic staff.
? To teach students how to communicate research in various formats (e.g. conference poster, writing manuscript for peer review journal, oral presentation).

outcome: 1. Demonstrate thorough knowledge of neurodiversity and development, both from the point of view of diagnosed neurodevelopmental conditions, and variation in developmental trajectories across the whole population.  (Applicable to the following qualifications: PGCert; PGDip; MSc Developmental Science and Neurodiversity )

2. Demonstrate skills for research on neurodiversity, taking account of the priorities and perspectives of relevant stakeholders, and how these interact with the practice of scientific research. (Applicable to the following qualifications: PGCert; PGDip; MSc Developmental Science and Neurodiversity )

3. Demonstrate knowledge and understanding for research on development and change across the full human lifespan. (Applicable to the following qualifications: PGCert; PGDip; MSc Developmental Science and Neurodiversity )
4. Scientific principles and methodologies for a broad range of research. (Applicable to the following qualifications: PGCert; PGDip; MSc Developmental Science and Neurodiversity )

assessment: Unseen examinations, Essay assignments, Problem solving exercises, Learning logs/diaries, Exhibitions/poster displays, Group projects, Independent projects, Oral presentations.

3. Integrate and critically evaluate scientific and stakeholder perspectives (Applicable to the following qualifications: PGCert; PGDip; MSc Developmental Science and Neurodiversity)

aims: The Birmingham Award with Distinction / The Birmingham Dubai Award with Distinction is a co-curricular programme that students undertake alongside their degree to develop, recognise, and articulate the attributes that they have developed at Birmingham, in preparation for the graduate recruitment and development processes.

The programme offers a flexible approach to skill development through the formal recognition of both on-and off campus extra-curricular activities, including those from all Colleges, Professional Services, and the Guild of Students.

This provision includes quality-assured structured teaching sessions that allow a learner to explore and develop a deeper understanding of a skill area through classroom-based teaching sessions, and digital education materials, co-created with employer partners.

Each activity recognised by The Birmingham Award will be required to identify the responsibilities of the role/activity and identify between one and four of the institutional Graduate Attributes that a student can develop as a result of engaging. A student will be required to participate in four activities, and for each activity, will need to identify an achievement or career progression goal from engagement, to be eligible to complete the award.

All students are required to complete a compulsory educational programme and associated summative assessments designed to prepare a learner for the graduate recruitment and development process. Each student receives personalised feedback on their assessment to ensure the transformative approach to the curriculum.
